</details>



This page documents the core mathematical operators, transformation layers, and Triton-accelerated kernels implemented in `src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/`. These modules form the fundamental building blocks of the BioMoA architecture, operating across single representations (`s`), pair representations (`z`), sequence/MSA representations (`m`), and atomic coordinates.

---

## 1. Attention with Pair Bias and Pair-Weighted Averaging

BioMoA relies heavily on AlphaFold2-style attention mechanisms where pairwise relationships explicitly modulate token-to-token interactions.

### `AttentionPairBias`
The `AttentionPairBias` module [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/attention_pair_bias.py:42-144]() performs multi-head self-attention on single features `s` ($[B\cdot M, N, c_s]$) augmented by pair representation biases `z` ($[B, N, N, c_z]$). The projection of `z` to per-head biases is executed either via standard linear transformations or an efficient fused 2D convolution (`_proj_z_fused`) [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/attention_pair_bias.py:97-127]() when layer norm bias is disabled.

### `PairWeightedAveraging`
The `PairWeightedAveraging` class [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/pair_weighted_averaging.py:6-153]() updates MSA representations (`m`) using information from the pairwise representation tensor (`z`). It computes attention weights over the pair axis, applies gating via `proj_g`, and scales updates across multiple heads.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "AttentionPairBias & PairWeightedAveraging Data Flow"
        S_IN["s: [B*M, N, c_s]"] --> NORM_S["norm_s / LayerNorm"]
        NORM_S --> QKV["proj_qkv / Linear"]
        QKV --> SPLIT["Chunk Q, K, V"]
        
        Z_IN["z: [B, N, N, c_z]"] --> PROJ_Z["_proj_z_fused / LayerNorm + Linear"]
        PROJ_Z --> BIAS["Pair Bias [B, H, N, N]"]
        
        SPLIT --> ATTN["Softmax((Q @ K^T)/sqrt(d) + Bias)"]
        BIAS --> ATTN
        ATTN --> OUT_ATTN["Output Projection proj_o"]
        
        M_IN["m: [B, S, N, c_m]"] --> PWA["PairWeightedAveraging"]
        Z_IN --> PWA
        PWA --> OUT_PWA["Updated MSA Representation"]
    end
```
*Sources: [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/attention_pair_bias.py:42-144](), [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/pair_weighted_averaging.py:6-153]()*

---

## 2. Tensor Mixing and Message Passing

Pair representations are continuously refined using triangular update operations and position-wise MLPs.

### Triangle Multiplication
Triangle multiplication variants are registered under `TriMulVariant` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/triangle_multiplication.py:56-60]() supporting incoming and outgoing edge updates:
* `TriangleMultiplicationFull` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/triangle_multiplication.py:86-100](): Full materialization einsum implementation ($O(N^2 D)$).
* `TriangleMultiplicationCueq` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/triangle_multiplication.py:102-152](): cuEquivariance-backed fused Triton kernel.
* `TriangleMultiplicationCueqTiled` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/triangle_multiplication.py:170-395](): Tiled variant utilizing fused dual GEMM projections for large systems ($N > 3000$).

### `Transition` (SwiGLU MLP)
The `Transition` module [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/transition.py:16-91]() implements a SwiGLU gated two-layer feed-forward network. It supports optional pre-LayerNorm and chunked hidden-dimension execution during inference to minimize peak VRAM allocation.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Transition & Triangle Multiplication Architecture"
        X_IN["x: [B, N, N, dim]"] --> NORM_IN["norm_in / LayerNorm"]
        NORM_IN --> PROJ_IN["p_in & g_in (SwiGLU gating)"]
        PROJ_IN --> TRI_OP{{"Multiplication Direction"}}
        TRI_OP -- "Outgoing" --> OUT_G["einsum bikd, bjkd -> bijd"]
        TRI_OP -- "Incoming" --> INC_G["einsum bkid, bkjd -> bijd"]
        OUT_G --> NORM_OUT["norm_out / LayerNorm"]
        INC_G --> NORM_OUT
        NORM_OUT --> PROJ_OUT["p_out & g_out Projection"]
        PROJ_OUT --> X_OUT["Updated Pair Features"]
        
        X_IN2["Tensor x"] --> TRANS["Transition / SwiGLU"]
        TRANS --> FC1["fc1 (gated) & fc2"]
        FC1 --> SILU["F.silu"]
        SILU --> FC3["fc3 Output Projection"]
        FC3 --> TRANS_OUT["MLP Output"]
    end
```
*Sources: [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/transition.py:16-91](), [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/triangle_multiplication.py:56-177]()*

---

## 3. Outer Product Mean and Triton Acceleration

The Outer Product Mean (OPM) operator aggregates MSA statistics into pairwise representations.

### Variants and Registry
The OPM implementation uses a registry-based dispatch via `OPMVariant` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/outer_product_mean.py:27-30]():
* `OuterProductMeanVanilla` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/outer_product_mean.py:42-76](): Standard baseline computing full `einsum("bsic,bsjd->bijcd", a, b)` with an $O(N^2 C_H^2)$ memory footprint.
* `OuterProductMeanTritonMemorySaving` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/outer_product_mean.py:78-153](): Automatically invokes Triton-fused token-tiled kernels during inference on CUDA devices while falling back to vanilla einsum during training.

### Triton Fused Kernel (`_opm_fused_kernel`)
The underlying Triton kernel `_opm_fused_kernel` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/triton/opm.py:18-141]() computes tile-based contractions across MSA depth ($S$) without materializing the full intermediate outer product tensor in global memory.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "OPM_Execution_Pipeline"
        MSA["m: [B, S, N, C_in]"] --> NORM["LayerNorm & proj_ab"]
        NORM --> CHUNK["Chunk into a, b projections"]
        CHUNK --> DISPATCH{{"Device & Training Mode?"}}
        DISPATCH -- "Training or CPU" --> VANILLA["OuterProductMeanVanilla / einsum"]
        DISPATCH -- "Inference on CUDA" --> TRITON_OP["_TritonOPMFn.apply"]
        TRITON_OP --> KERNEL["_opm_fused_kernel / Triton JIT Kernel"]
        KERNEL --> REG_ACC["Tile-based Accumulation in Registers"]
        REG_ACC --> PROJ_O["proj_o Linear Projection"]
        VANILLA --> OUT["Pair Representation [B, N, N, C_out]"]
        PROJ_O --> OUT
    end
```
*Sources: [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/outer_product_mean.py:27-153](), [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/triton/opm.py:18-141]()*

---

## 4. Structural Interoperability: Atom and Token Operations

BioMoA maps between coarse-grained token features and atomic representations using index-based gather and scatter operations defined in `atom_token_ops.py`.

### Key Functions
* `broadcast_tokens_to_atoms` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/atom_token_ops.py:6-27](): Broadcasts per-token features (`[B*M, T, D]`) to atomic resolution via `atom_to_token_ids` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/atom_token_ops.py:8](), routing padding atoms to a dedicated zero-initialized token slot.
* `scatter_mean_atoms_to_tokens` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/atom_token_ops.py:29-55](): Aggregates atomic features back to token slots using `scatter_add_` in FP32 precision.
* `gather_center_tokens_from_atomic` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/atom_token_ops.py:57-76](): Extracts anchor atom coordinates per token using `token_center_atom_index` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/atom_token_ops.py:59]().
* `broadcast_token_pair_to_atom_window` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/atom_token_ops.py:78-128](): Expands token pair representations (`z`) onto sliding atomic windows for atomic-level attention layers.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Atom_Token_Interoperability_Mapping"
        TOK["per_token: [B*M, T, D]"] --> BROADCAST["broadcast_tokens_to_atoms"]
        ATOM_IDS["atom_to_token_ids & is_padded_atom"] --> BROADCAST
        BROADCAST --> ATOMS["per_atom: [B*M, N, D]"]
        
        ATOMS --> SCATTER["scatter_mean_atoms_to_tokens"]
        SCATTER --> TOK_OUT["Aggregated Token Features"]
        
        ATOMS --> GATHER_CENTER["gather_center_tokens_from_atomic"]
        CENTER_IDX["token_center_atom_index"] --> GATHER_CENTER
        GATHER_CENTER --> TOKEN_CENTERS["Token Center Features"]
        
        Z_PAIR["z: [B, T, T, D]"] --> WINDOW_BC["broadcast_token_pair_to_atom_window"]
        ATOM_IDS --> WINDOW_BC
        WINDOW_BC --> WINDOW_OUT["Sliding Atom-Pair Window Features"]
    end
```
*Sources: [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/atom_token_ops.py:6-128]()*

---

## 5. Regularization and Utility Operators

### Axis-Wise Dropout
To prevent overfitting while preserving structural correlations along specific sequence or pair axes, BioMoA implements axis-wise dropout in `dropout.py` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/dropout.py:3-70]().

* `get_axiswise_dropout_mask` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/dropout.py:8-56](): Constructs rank-4 broadcast dropout masks (`[B, 1, Y, 1]` for column-wise or `[B, X, 1, 1]` for row-wise dropping) [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/dropout.py:41](). Masks are scaled by inverted dropout factors ($1 / (1 - \text{dropout})$) [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/dropout.py:20-21]() to avoid evaluation-time corrections.
* `apply_axiswise_dropout` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/dropout.py:58-70](): Applies the generated mask conditional on training mode.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Axiswise_Dropout_Workflow"
        TENSOR_IN["Tensor z: [B, X, Y, D]"] --> CHECK{{"Training Mode & Rate > 0?"}}
        CHECK -- "False" --> RETURN_IN["Return x unchanged"]
        CHECK -- "True" --> MODE{{"columnwise flag"}}
        MODE -- "True" --> COL_MASK["Mask shape [B, 1, Y, 1] (drops entire columns)"]
        MODE -- "False" --> ROW_MASK["Mask shape [B, X, 1, 1] (drops entire rows)"]
        COL_MASK --> SCALE["Inverted Scaling: 1 / (1 - dropout)"]
        ROW_MASK --> SCALE
        SCALE --> MULT["Elementwise multiplication with x"]
        MULT --> DROPOUT_OUT["Regularized Tensor"]
    end
```
*Sources: [src/bioemu2/biomoa/ops/dropout.py:8-70]()*

---

# Page: Model Utilities: Precision, Tiling, Strategy

# Model Utilities: Precision, Tiling, Strategy

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/__init__.py](src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/__init__.py)
- [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/feature_converter.py](src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/feature_converter.py)
- [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py](src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py)
- [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/strategy.py](src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/strategy.py)
- [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/tiling.py](src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/tiling.py)
- [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/warnings.py](src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/warnings.py)

</details>



The `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/` package provides low-level supporting infrastructure for the BioMoA score model stack. These utilities handle feature transformations between dense structure representations and model-consumable flat dictionaries, manage fine-grained matrix multiplication precision knobs, instantiate model sub-modules dynamically via a centralized strategy factory, resolve memory-saving tiling and chunking configurations with automatic variant switching, and suppress expected third-party deprecation warnings.

---

## 1. Feature Conversion (`feature_converter.py`)

The BioMoA score model consumes flat feature dictionaries rather than nested object hierarchies. The module `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/feature_converter.py` bridges dense structure batches (`BatchAllAtomStructure`) to flat tensor dictionaries expected by the transformer trunk and its sub-modules [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/feature_converter.py:1-24].

### Key Functions and Behavior
- **`convert_densebatch_to_dictionary(dense_batch, *, build_pair_features=True)`**: Extracts zero-copy tensor references from `dense_batch.to_dict()` and transforms specific keys (boolean casts, derived token features, padding sentinels, and contact conditioning fallbacks) [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/feature_converter.py:19-51].
- **Index Sentinels**: Uses `INDEX_PAD_VALUE: int = -1` for index-valued fields to ensure unmasked padding values fail loudly via scatter out-of-bounds errors rather than silently aliasing index `0` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/feature_converter.py:13-16, 86].
- **Contact Conditioning Fallback**: If `build_pair_features` is active and contact conditioning is absent, it invokes `make_unspecified_contact_conditioning` and `make_unspecified_contact_threshold` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/feature_converter.py:58-66].
- **Derived Features**: Gathers residue types and indices from atom-level tensors via `token_center_atom_index`, computes symmetric `token_bonds`, and transposes MSA features to depth-first layout [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/feature_converter.py:75-120].

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["BatchAllAtomStructure"] --> B["convert_densebatch_to_dictionary"]
    B --> C["TensorReferenceExtraction"]
    B --> D["BooleanCastMasks"]
    B --> E["ContactConditioningFallback"]
    B --> F["DerivedTokenFeatures"]
    B --> G["MSATransposeAndPadding"]
    C --> H["FlatFeatureDictionary"]
    D --> H
    E --> H
    F --> H
    G --> H

    sub-sources-1
    Sources: src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/feature_converter.py:1-122
```

Sources: `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/feature_converter.py:1-122`

---

## 2. Precision Configuration and Matmul Knobs (`precision.py`)

Matrix multiplication precision in kernel sub-modules (such as outer product mean and triangle multiplication) is governed by `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py:1-19].

### Precision Rules and Resolution
- **Knob Values**: Supports `"ieee"`, `"tf32"`, and `"tf32x3"` (with `cueq` TriMul also permitting `None`) [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py:1-5].
- **Variant Validation**: Maps specific precision knobs to compatible execution variants via `VARIANTS_WITH_PRECISION_KNOB` and `DEFAULT_PRECISION_KEYS` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py:26-41].
- **`resolve_precision_cfg(precision_cfg, *, site, variant)`**: Traverses a nested precision configuration dictionary (e.g., `msa_module.opm_matmul_precision`), falling back to variant defaults if `null` is specified, and warns if an incompatible variant attempts to claim a knob without switching variants [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py:44-85].

Sources: `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py:1-85`

---

## 3. Strategy Factory and Dynamic Instantiation (`strategy.py`)

The strategy module `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/strategy.py` supplies a centralized factory for instantiating variant-based sub-modules [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/strategy.py:1-5].

### The `make()` Factory
- **`make(registry, variant, *, matmul_precision=None, **kwargs)`**: Looks up `variant` (string or enum) in a module registry dictionary, dynamically imports the target module path, inspects the class signature for `matmul_precision`, injects it if supported, and passes remaining `**kwargs` to the constructor [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/strategy.py:13-50].
- **Silent Ignoring**: Variants that do not accept a precision knob (e.g., vanilla or transition modules) silently ignore `matmul_precision`, enabling uniform parameter passing across kernel families [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/strategy.py:21-27].

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["CallerConfig"] -->|RegistryAndVariant| B["strategy.make"]
    B --> C["LookupRegistryEntry"]
    C --> D["ImportModuleAndClass"]
    D --> E["InspectConstructorSignature"]
    E -->|SupportsMatmulPrecision| F["InjectMatmulPrecision"]
    E -->|DoesNotSupport| G["SkipPrecisionKwarg"]
    F --> H["InstantiateModule"]
    G --> H
    H --> I["nn.ModuleInstance"]

    sub-sources-3
    Sources: src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/strategy.py:1-50
```

Sources: `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/strategy.py:1-50`

---

## 4. Memory Tiling and Chunking (`tiling.py`)

To control memory consumption during long-sequence or deep-MSA inference, `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/tiling.py` parses, validates, and auto-corrects tiling configurations (`tiling_cfg`) [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/tiling.py:1-32].

### Key Data Structures and Functions
- **Module Known Keys**: `MODULE_KNOWN_KEYS` defines which tiling keys are legal for specific consumers (e.g., `BioMoaCModel` vs `PairMixerSequenceEmbedder`) [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/tiling.py:61-64].
- **Global Dominance**: Global keys (`tile_size` and `chunk_size`) override all corresponding `*_tile_size` or `*_chunk_size` entries [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/tiling.py:39-42, 131-165].
- **Variant Auto-Switching**: `resolve_tiling_cfg` checks `TILING_KEY_VARIANT_REQUIREMENTS`. If a non-default tile or chunk size is requested on an incompatible variant, it automatically switches the variant to the corresponding entry in `PREFERRED_VARIANT_FOR_TILING` (e.g., switching to `triton_memory_saving` for `opm_tile_size`) and emits a warning [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/tiling.py:69-94, 131-171].

Sources: `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/tiling.py:1-171`

---

## 5. Warning Management (`warnings.py`)

Third-party dependencies (such as `cuequivariance`) occasionally trigger deprecation warnings at import time that cannot be directly modified within BioEmu2. The module `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/warnings.py` isolates these warnings [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/warnings.py:1-28].

- **`suppress_cuequivariance_jit_deprecation()`**: A context manager that catches `torch.jit.script` deprecation warnings matching `_TORCH_JIT_SCRIPT_DEPRECATIONS` and suppresses them during third-party library initialization [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/warnings.py:5-28].

Sources: `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/warnings.py:1-28`

---

# Page: Sampling, Denoising and Steering

# Sampling, Denoising and Steering

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/propagation.md](docs/propagation.md)
- [docs/sampling.md](docs/sampling.md)
- [docs/steering.md](docs/steering.md)

</details>



The sampling, denoising, and steering subsystem of BioEmu2 coordinates the transformation of noise and conditioning inputs into physical biomolecular structures. It encompasses Elucidating Diffusion Models (EDM) samplers, task-specific operational modes, inference-time physical and geometric steering potentials, spatial contact conditioning, and implicit transfer operator time propagation. 

This is a parent page providing a high-level overview of the denoising stack. For deep technical implementations, see the child pages:
- [Denoising Samplers and EDM](#4.1)
- [Inference-Time Steering and Potentials](#4.2)
- [Contact Conditioning](#4.3)
- [Time Propagation (Implicit Transfer Operators)](#4.4)

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["NaturalLanguage:EquilibriumSampling"] --> B["CodeEntity:EmuSession.sample"]
    B --> C["CodeEntity:EDMSampler"]
    C --> D["CodeEntity:ScoreModel"]
    
    E["NaturalLanguage:StructurePrediction"] --> F["CodeEntity:EmuSession.mode='structure'"]
    F --> C

    Sources: [docs/sampling.md:107-120]()
```

## Denoising Samplers and EDM

BioEmu2 frames generation as a stochastic diffusion process over atomic coordinates governed by score-based models [docs/sampling.md:147-151](). The foundational sampling loops are implemented around Elucidating Diffusion Models (EDM) principles. Depending on user intent, the system operates in either **equilibrium** mode or **structure prediction** mode. Equilibrium mode targets an unbiased representation of the Boltzmann ensemble, whereas structure prediction applies heuristic sharpening to produce single, highly folded reference geometries [docs/sampling.md:107-120]().

To handle rotational and translational invariance during the reverse diffusion trajectory, the denoising engine integrates specialized modules for augmentation, rigid body alignment, and context-parallel synchronization. 

For full details on the underlying samplers, noise schedules, alignment routines, and mode configurations, see [Denoising Samplers and EDM](#4.1).

Sources: [docs/sampling.md:107-151](), [docs/propagation.md:163-165]()

## Inference-Time Steering and Potentials

To influence generated conformational ensembles without retraining the underlying model, BioEmu2 provides an inference-time steering subpackage [docs/steering.md:16-22](). Steering modifies the sampling trajectory by tilting the base model distribution toward a user-defined target distribution using scalar energy potentials $U(x)$ [docs/steering.md:34-42](). 

The package supports gradient-based guidance and Feynman-Kac particle resampling via specialized sampler classes such as `GuidedFKSampler` and `FKCSampler` [docs/steering.md:78-81](). Default physicality potentials automatically penalize atomic clashes, incorrect bond lengths, and distorted geometry, ensuring chemically sensible outputs even for large macromolecular systems [docs/steering.md:61-66]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["NaturalLanguage:PhysicalitySteering"] --> B["CodeEntity:GuidedFKSampler"]
    A2["NaturalLanguage:ParticleResampling"] --> C["CodeEntity:FKCSampler"]
    B --> D["CodeEntity:Potential"]
    C --> D
    D --> E["CodeEntity:BondLengthPotential"]
    D --> F["CodeEntity:ClashPotential"]

    Sources: [docs/steering.md:78-96]()
```

For comprehensive documentation on custom potentials, RDKit constraints, and sampler configurations, see [Inference-Time Steering and Potentials](#4.2).

Sources: [docs/steering.md:16-96]()

## Contact Conditioning

Spatial constraints and contact maps can be passed directly into the generation pipeline to restrict or guide the layout of polymer chains [docs/sampling.md:143-148](). Unlike post-hoc steering potentials, contact conditioning injects distance or pairing constraints directly into the feature representation and trunk conditioning layers prior to diffusion sampling [docs/steering.md:28-33]().

This mechanism enables users to enforce experimentally derived interaction restraints (such as cross-linking mass spectrometry or mutagenesis data) while allowing the emulator to generate physically relaxed tertiary structures around those constraints.

For further information on contact map representations, conditioning APIs, and constraint examples, see [Contact Conditioning](#4.3).

Sources: [docs/sampling.md:143-148](), [docs/steering.md:28-33]()

## Time Propagation (Implicit Transfer Operators)

Beyond unconditioned generation and equilibrium sampling, BioEmu2 supports time propagation using implicit transfer operators. Given a starting conformation $x_0$, the model can sample future endpoints $x_\tau$ at a specified lag time $\tau$ (`lag_time_ns`), effectively simulating molecular dynamics over extended timescales without stepping through continuous short-time integration paths [docs/propagation.md:16-28]().

The propagation framework supports single-endpoint sampling per frame, multi-endpoint branching, and time-ordered trajectory construction via `simulate_trajectory()` [docs/propagation.md:16-20, 150-162](). Reusing trunk embeddings across sequential propagation steps ensures computational efficiency during extended temporal simulations [docs/propagation.md:26-28].

For detailed guides on lag-time configuration, external coordinate mapping, and trajectory generation workflows, see [Time Propagation (Implicit Transfer Operators)](#4.4).

Sources: [docs/propagation.md:16-28, 150-162]()

---

# Page: Denoising Samplers and EDM

# Denoising Samplers and EDM

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/sampling.md](docs/sampling.md)
- [src/bioemu2/biomoa/models/edm_schedule.py](src/bioemu2/biomoa/models/edm_schedule.py)
- [src/bioemu2/biomoa/modules/diffusion.py](src/bioemu2/biomoa/modules/diffusion.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page covers the technical implementation of the denoising pipeline in BioEmu2, focusing on the `src/bioemu2/denoising` subpackage and its integration with the Elucidated Diffusion Model (EDM) framework. It details the noise schedules, sampling algorithms, auxiliary utilities (`augmentation`, `rigid_align`, `cp_sync`), and the operational differences between structure prediction and equilibrium sampling modes.

Sources: `src/bioemu2/biomoa/models/edm_schedule.py:1-87](), [docs/sampling.md:1-120]()`

---

## 1. Elucidated Diffusion Model (EDM) Schedule and Scaling

BioEmu2 implements the score-based diffusion formulation introduced by Karras et al., adapted for biomolecular atomic coordinates. The core scaling functions and noise conditioning are defined in `src/bioemu2/biomoa/models/edm_schedule.py` via the `EDMSchedule` class.

### Key Scaling Coefficients

The denoised coordinates ($\mathbf{x}_{\text{denoised}}$) are reconstructed from noisy inputs ($\mathbf{x}_{\text{noisy}}$) and the network prediction ($\mathbf{f}_{\theta}$) using preconditioning coefficients that depend on the noise level $\sigma$:

$$\mathbf{x}_{\text{denoised}} = c_{\text{skip}}(\sigma) \mathbf{x}_{\text{noisy}} + c_{\text{out}}(\sigma) \mathbf{f}_{\theta}(c_{\text{in}}(\sigma) \mathbf{x}_{\text{noisy}}, \sigma)$$

| Coefficient | Function | Mathematical Definition | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `c_skip` | `EDMSchedule.c_skip(sigma)` | $\frac{\sigma_{\text{data}}^2}{\sigma^2 + \sigma_{\text{data}}^2}$ | Retains a proportion of the noisy input signal. |
| `c_out` | `EDMSchedule.c_out(sigma)` | $\frac{\sigma \sigma_{\text{data}}}{\sqrt{\sigma_{\text{data}}^2 + \sigma^2}}$ | Scales the neural network's coordinate update. |
| `c_in` | `EDMSchedule.c_in(sigma)` | $\frac{1}{\sqrt{\sigma^2 + \sigma_{\text{data}}^2}}$ | Normalizes input atomic coordinates to unit variance. |
| `c_noise`| `EDMSchedule.c_noise(sigma)` | $\frac{1}{4} \ln\left(\frac{\sigma}{\sigma_{\text{data}}}\right)$ | Computes noise level conditioning for time/sigma embeddings. |

The default data standard deviation is set to $\sigma_{\text{data}} = 16.0$ Å, with noise bounds ranging from $\sigma_{\min} = 0.0004$ to $\sigma_{\max} = 160.0$.

```mermaid
title "EDMSchedule Data Flow and Coordinate Transformation"

graph TD
    InputCoords["Input Coordinates x_noisy"] --> Cin["EDMSchedule.c_in(sigma)"]
    InputCoords --> Cskip["EDMSchedule.c_skip(sigma)"]
    Sigma["Noise Level sigma"] --> Cin
    Sigma --> Cskip
    Sigma --> Cout["EDMSchedule.c_out(sigma)"]
    Sigma --> Cnoise["EDMSchedule.c_noise(sigma)"]
    
    Cin --> Model["DualStreamDiffusionModule.forward()"]
    Cnoise --> Model
    Model --> NetOut["Network Output f_theta"]
    
    NetOut --> Cout
    Cout --> Combine["Linear Combination"]
    Cskip --> Combine
    InputCoords --> Combine
    
    Combine --> DenoisedCoords["Output Coordinates x_denoised"]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
```

Sources: `[src/bioemu2/biomoa/models/edm_schedule.py:1-86](), [src/bioemu2/biomoa/modules/diffusion.py:1-135]()`

---

## 2. Samplers and Time Discretization

The sampling engine orchestrates the reverse SDE/ODE integration from pure noise ($\sigma_{\max}$) down to data scale ($\sigma_{\min}$). 

### Sampler Execution Pipeline

Samplers in `src/bioemu2/denoising/samplers.py` manage discretization schedules, stochasticity parameters (such as stochastic Langevin-like noise additions), and step scaling heuristics.

```mermaid
title "Sampler Execution Flow in Code Entity Space"

graph TD
    Session["EmuSession.sample()"] --> SamplerEntry["samplers.sample_loop()"]
    SamplerEntry --> ScheduleGen["Generate Sigma Schedule (t__steps)"]
    
    ScheduleGen --> Loop{For each sigma_i}
    Loop --> PredictScore["DualStreamDiffusionModule()"]
    PredictScore --> ApplyEDM["EDMSchedule (c_skip, c_out, c_in)"]
    ApplyEDM --> EulerStep["Discretization Step (Euler / Heun)"]
    EulerStep --> CheckCP["cp_sync.synchronize_ranks()"]
    CheckCP --> Align["rigid_align.kabsch_align()"]
    Align --> NextSigma{More steps?}
    NextSigma -- Yes --> Loop
    NextSigma -- No --> ReturnSamples["Return Tensor of Conformations"]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
```

Sources: `[src/bioemu2/biomoa/modules/diffusion.py:1-160](), [docs/sampling.md:72-120]()`

---

## 3. Equilibrium vs. Structure Modes

BioEmu2 distinguishes between two distinct operational modes tailored for different biophysical applications. These modes modify parameters like step scaling (`step_scale`) and sampling noise during execution.

| Mode | CLI Subcommand | Session Configuration | Target Objective | Key Hyperparameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Structure Prediction** | `bioemu2 predict-structure` | `EmuSession(..., mode="structure")` | High-accuracy individual folded structure | Heuristic sharpening with `step_scale = 1.5` |
| **Equilibrium Sampling** | `bioemu2 sample-equilibrium`| `EmuSession(..., mode="equilibrium")`| Broad thermodynamic conformational ensemble | `step_scale = 1.0`, unsharpened trajectory |

### Mode Selection via Python API

When initializing an `EmuSession`, the mode string determines internal diffusion step multipliers and output configurations:

```python
from bioemu2 import EmuSession, System, load_model

system = System.from_pdb_id("1AKE")
model = load_model()

# Structure prediction mode (applies heuristic step scaling)
struct_session = EmuSession(system, model=model, mode="structure")

# Equilibrium sampling mode (standard thermodynamic path)
eq_session = EmuSession(system, model=model, mode="equilibrium")
```

Sources: `[docs/sampling.md:107-120]()`

---

## 4. Supporting Denoiser Utilities

The denoising subsystem relies on several specialized modules for coordinate manipulation, symmetry, and parallel execution:

* **`augmentation`**: Applies random spatial rotations and translations during training or data preprocessing to ensure SO(3) invariance.
* **`rigid_align`**: Implements root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) minimization routines (such as the Kabsch algorithm) to superimpose generated frames onto reference topologies or input templates.
* **`cp_sync`**: Manages tensor synchronization across multiple GPUs when executing context-parallel sampling runs for large macromolecules.

Sources: `[docs/sampling.md:90-96]()`

---

# Page: Inference-Time Steering and Potentials

# Inference-Time Steering and Potentials

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/potentials.md](docs/potentials.md)
- [docs/steering.md](docs/steering.md)
- [examples/improve_disulfide_physicality_with_steering.py](examples/improve_disulfide_physicality_with_steering.py)
- [examples/tilt_a_sample_distribution_with_steering.py](examples/tilt_a_sample_distribution_with_steering.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The steering subpackage (`bioemu2.denoising.steering`, comprising modules such as `edm_steered`, `edm_fkc`, `potentials`, `rdkit_constraints`, and `geometry_topology`) provides tools for modifying the target distribution sampled by the biomolecular emulator foundation model at inference time without retraining [docs/steering.md:16-17]. This page details the implementation architecture, core classes, mathematical formulation of tilted distributions, default physicality potentials, and custom potential definitions [docs/potentials.md:3-5, docs/steering.md:34-42].

Sources: `docs/potentials.md:1-10`, `docs/steering.md:16-22`

---

## Mathematical Foundation and Target Distribution

Let $x$ denote the atomic coordinates and $p_{\mathrm{base}}(x)$ be the probability distribution sampled by the unsteered base model for a given system and conditioning [docs/steering.md:36-37]. Given a steering potential $U(x)$, inference-time steering aims to sample from the **tilted distribution** [docs/steering.md:37-42]:

$$
p_{\mathrm{target}}(x) \propto p_{\mathrm{base}}(x)\exp[-U(x)]
$$

The overall energy $U(x)$ can be decomposed into a sum of sub-potentials, $U(x) = \sum_i U_i(x)$, where each sub-potential $U_i(x)$ favors a specific geometric or physical property [docs/steering.md:54-55]. Smaller energy values indicate more favorable configurations [docs/potentials.md:5].

Sources: `docs/steering.md:34-60`

---

## Steering Subpackage Architecture and Modules

The steering framework bridges high-level objectives with low-level samplers through distinct functional components. The following diagram illustrates the bridge from natural language steering concepts to code entities in the `bioemu2` codebase.

### Natural Language to Code Entity Mapping

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Concepts"
        A[""Unsteered Diffusion""]
        B[""Gradient-Based Steering (FK)""]
        C[""Feynman-Kac Correctors (FKC)""]
        D[""Potential Energy Objective""]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        E["bioemu2.EDMSampler"]
        F["bioemu2.GuidedFKSampler"]
        G["bioemu2.FKCSampler"]
        H["bioemu2.Potential"]
    end

    A --> E
    B --> F
    C --> G
    D --> H
```
Sources: `docs/steering.md:128-156`, `examples/tilt_a_sample_distribution_with_steering.py:32-39`

The sampling algorithms and steering mechanisms interact with system topologies and coordinate tensors during reverse diffusion.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Execution Flow"
        I["SystemTopology"] --> J["Potential.prepare(system)"]
        J --> K["EmuSession.sample()"]
        K --> L["GuidedFKSampler or FKCSampler"]
        L --> M["Potential.__call__(coords_angstrom, t)"]
        M --> N["Gradient Computation / Resampling"]
    end
```
Sources: `docs/potentials.md:3-5`, `docs/steering.md:85-117`

Sources: `docs/steering.md:128-156`, `docs/potentials.md:3-10`

---

## Physicality Potentials

Default physicality potentials are instantiated via `get_default_potentials()` and utilized by `GuidedFKSampler` and `FKCSampler` (as well as CLI options `--sampler edm_gd`, `edm_fk`, and `edm_fkc`) [docs/potentials.md:31-34, 43-46]. These potentials penalize unrealistic geometry such as clashes, broken bonds, and valence violations [docs/potentials.md:48].

| Potential Class | What it Penalizes | Code Reference / Module |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BondLengthPotential` | Bond lengths outside reference bounds | `bioemu2.denoising.steering.potentials` [docs/potentials.md:13-20] |
| `BondAnglePotential` | Bond angles outside reference bounds | `bioemu2.denoising.steering.potentials` [docs/potentials.md:13-21] |
| `InterChainVDWOverlapPotential` | Van der Waals overlaps between atoms in different chains | `bioemu2.denoising.steering.potentials` [docs/potentials.md:13-22] |
| `IntraChainVDWOverlapPotential` | Van der Waals overlaps within polymer chains | `bioemu2.denoising.steering.potentials` [docs/potentials.md:13-23] |
| `PolymerLocalClashPotential` | Short-range inter-residue clashes (2-3 bonds apart) | `bioemu2.denoising.steering.potentials` [docs/potentials.md:13-24] |
| `SymmetricChainCOMPotential` | Centres of mass of equivalent chains getting too close | `bioemu2.denoising.steering.potentials` [docs/potentials.md:13-25] |
| `PoseBustersPotential` | Violations of ligand distance bounds | `bioemu2.denoising.steering.potentials` [docs/potentials.md:13-26] |
| `ChiralAtomPotential` | Incorrect chirality at ligand stereocentres | `bioemu2.denoising.steering.potentials` [docs/potentials.md:13-27] |
| `StereoBondPotential` | Incorrect ligand bond stereochemistry | `bioemu2.denoising.steering.potentials` [docs/potentials.md:13-28] |
| `PlanarBondPotential` | Non-planar ligand bonds that should be planar | `bioemu2.denoising.steering.potentials` [docs/potentials.md:13-29] |

Specialized potentials include `ContactPotential` (penalizing atom pairs exceeding contact distances) and `TemplateReferencePotential` (penalizing deviations from a rigid-aligned reference template) [docs/potentials.md:36-39].

Sources: `docs/potentials.md:11-40`

---

## Custom Potentials and Parameter Scheduling

Users can define custom objectives by subclassing `Potential`, implementing `prepare(system)` for system-specific initialization, and `__call__(coords_angstrom, *, t)` to compute scalar energies per structure [docs/potentials.md:104-107]. 

### Example: Custom Potential Implementation

```python
class TerminiTargetExpPotential(Potential):
    """Energy = well * (Cα-Cα distance - target)², with distances in Å."""

    def __init__(self, target_angstrom: float) -> None:
        self.target_angstrom = target_angstrom
        self.well = 2
        self.atom_indices: tuple[int, int] | None = None

    def prepare(self, system) -> None:
        ca_indices = [atom.index for atom in system.topology.atoms if atom.name == "CA"]
        self.atom_indices = (ca_indices[0], ca_indices[-1])

    def __call__(self, coords_angstrom: torch.Tensor, *, t: float) -> torch.Tensor:
        start, end = self.atom_indices
        distance = torch.linalg.vector_norm(
            coords_angstrom[:, start] - coords_angstrom[:, end], dim=-1
        )
        return self.well * (distance - self.target_angstrom).pow(2)
```
Sources: `examples/tilt_a_sample_distribution_with_steering.py:64-81`

### Parameter Configuration

For `GuidedFKSampler`, parameter mappings control potential influence [docs/potentials.md:80-83]:
* `guidance_weight`: Scales the potential coordinate gradient during guidance [docs/potentials.md:85-87].
* `guidance_interval`: Applies the gradient every $N$ inner steps [docs/potentials.md:85-88].
* `resampling_weight`: Scales the potential contribution to reweighting/resampling [docs/potentials.md:85-89].

Scheduled values can change across denoising via `ParameterSchedule` variants such as `PiecewiseStepFunction`, `ExponentialInterpolation`, or `LinearInterpolation`, where normalized time runs from $t=1$ (high noise) to $t=0$ (clean endpoint) [docs/potentials.md:91-95].

Sources: `docs/potentials.md:80-97`, `examples/tilt_a_sample_distribution_with_steering.py:64-81`

---

# Page: Contact Conditioning

# Contact Conditioning

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [examples/sample_protein_ligand_constraints.py](examples/sample_protein_ligand_constraints.py)
- [examples/sample_protein_protein_constraints.py](examples/sample_protein_protein_constraints.py)
- [src/bioemu2/conditioning/__init__.py](src/bioemu2/conditioning/__init__.py)
- [src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py](src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py)
- [src/bioemu2/conditioning/method.py](src/bioemu2/conditioning/method.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The `src/bioemu2/conditioning` subpackage provides data structures, token maps, and conditioning matrices required to bias biomolecular complex and equilibrium predictions towards user-specified spatial constraints (such as protein-ligand binding pockets or protein-protein interfaces) and experimental sampling modes. This page details the internal representation of contact classes, tensor conditioning builders, experimental method type registries, and practical constraint specification patterns derived from example scripts.

Sources:
- `src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py` [src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py:1-82]()
- `src/bioemu2/conditioning/method.py` [src/bioemu2/conditioning/method.py:1-44]()

---

## 1. Conditioning Classes and Method Registries

BioEmu2 classifies pairwise interactions and experimental contexts using fixed integer mapping dictionaries. In `src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py`, `contact_conditioning_info` maps symbolic conditioning categories to integer identifiers [src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py:8-14] (`UNSPECIFIED`, `UNSELECTED`, `POCKET>BINDER`, `BINDER>POCKET`, and `CONTACT`).

Similarly, `src/bioemu2/conditioning/method.py` defines `method_types_ids`, mapping experimental or computational source descriptors (e.g., X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, molecular dynamics) to normalized integer categories [src/bioemu2/conditioning/method.py:8-37], alongside the `SamplingMode` literal (`"structure"` or `"equilibrium"`) [src/bioemu2/conditioning/method.py:3-5].

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["UserConstraintDefinition"] --> B["contact_conditioning_info"]
    B --> C["UNSPECIFIED: 0"]
    B --> D["UNSELECTED: 1"]
    B --> E["CONTACT: 4"]
    F["SamplingContext"] --> G["method_types_ids"]
    G --> H["X-RAY DIFFRACTION: 0"]
    G --> I["MD: 4"]
```
Sources:
- `src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py` [src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py:8-17]()
- `src/bioemu2/conditioning/method.py` [src/bioemu2/conditioning/method.py:5-39]()

---

## 2. Matrix Generation and Feature Utilities

When no explicit contacts are provided, BioEmu2 initializes neutral conditioning tensors via dedicated factory functions. The function `make_unspecified_contact_conditioning` constructs a `(T, T, C)` one-hot tensor filled with `UNSPECIFIED` flags for all token pairs [src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py:19-42]. The companion function `make_unspecified_contact_threshold` builds a zero-valued `(T, T)` float tensor representing distance thresholds [src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py:44-60].

During batch processing, `count_revealed_contacts` extracts active constraint counts from batch collations by evaluating the upper triangle of the `CONTACT` channel mask [src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py:63-82].

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["make_unspecified_contact_conditioning"] --> B["Tensor_T_T_C"]
    C["make_unspecified_contact_threshold"] --> D["Tensor_T_T"]
    E["count_revealed_contacts"] --> F["UpperTriangleExtraction"]
    F --> G["PerSampleContactCount"]
```
Sources:
- `src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py` [src/bioemu2/conditioning/contact.py:19-82]()

---

## 4. Constraint Examples and Specification Patterns

Contact conditioning is supplied to `EmuSession` as a list of `Contact` objects linking two `ContactToken` endpoints with maximum distance limits [examples/sample_protein_ligand_constraints.py:88-103, examples/sample_protein_protein_constraints.py:53-60].

For protein-ligand interactions (e.g., human serum albumin with ibuprofen), protein residues anchor via Cα tokens while ligands anchor via named atoms [examples/sample_protein_ligand_constraints.py:55-57, 93-103]. For protein-protein complexes (e.g., the 1TEN design system), residues across chains are paired with specific Cα–Cα distance thresholds [examples/sample_protein_protein_constraints.py:39-60].

```mermaid

        CE3["EmuSession contacts_parameter"]
    end

    NL2 --> CE1
    CE1 --> CE2
    CE2 --> CE3
```

# Page: Time Propagation (Implicit Transfer Operators)

# Time Propagation (Implicit Transfer Operators)

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/propagation.md](docs/propagation.md)
- [examples/simulate_a_trajectory.py](examples/simulate_a_trajectory.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page details the time propagation framework in BioEmu2, which implements implicit transfer operators to sample future conformations (`x_t`) at a given time lag (`lag_time_ns`) from a starting conformation (`x0`). Unlike equilibrium sampling, propagation captures temporal evolution and kinetics over lag times ranging from 1 ns to 1 µs.

Sources: `docs/propagation.md:1-29`

---

## Core Concepts: Lag Times and Endpoints
Propagation in BioEmu2 models conditional distributions over future states given a starting structure. 
- **Endpoints**: Each propagation step generates an independent endpoint at time $t = \text{lag\_time\_ns}$, rather than recording physical intermediate steps of a continuous path.
- **Lag Time Range**: Optimal performance occurs with lag times from 1 ns to 1000 ns (the regime heavily represented during training). For multi-millisecond timescales, equilibrium sampling should be used instead.
- **Embedding Reuse**: Using `EmuSession.propagate()` preserves trunk embeddings in memory across multiple propagation calls for the same molecular system.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "NaturalLanguageSpace"
        A["StartingConformation"] --> B["TimeLagSelection"]
        B --> C["EndpointPrediction"]
    end
    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        D["System"] --> E["EmuSession.propagate()"]
        E --> F["save_frames()"]
    end
    A -.-> D
    B -.-> E
    C -.-> F

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:black,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 1: Conceptual mapping between natural language propagation steps and BioEmu2 classes.*

Sources: `docs/propagation.md:16-29`

---

## Command Line Interface (CLI) Workflow
The CLI provides subcommands to initialize equilibrium conformations and propagate them forward in time.

### Single and Batch Propagation via CLI
To sample a starting conformation and propagate it at a 1 ns lag:
```bash
bioemu2 sample-equilibrium --pdb-id 1AKE --num-samples 1 --out outputs/adk-start
bioemu2 propagate --x0-cif outputs/adk-start/topology.cif --num-samples 8 --lag-time-ns 1 --out outputs/adk-propagated
```

To use an external CIF file along with a custom system specification YAML:
```bash
bioemu2 propagate --x0-cif initial.cif --system system.yaml --num-samples 8 --lag-time-ns 1 --out outputs/from-external-cif
```

- **Atom Ordering**: The CLI expects starting atoms to match the system order precisely; atoms cannot be reordered automatically during direct CIF ingestion unless mapped beforehand.
- **Outputs**: Generates `samples.xtc`, `topology.cif`, and `physicality.json` detailing physicality metrics for each generated endpoint.

Sources: `docs/propagation.md:30-89`

---

## Python API: EmuSession and Trajectory Simulation
The Python API allows granular control over session states, starting structures, and multi-step rollout trajectories.

### EmuSession Propagation
```python
system = System.from_pdb_id("1AKE")
model = load_model()
emu = EmuSession(system, model=model, mode="equilibrium")
x0 = emu.sample(num_samples=1)
x_tau = emu.propagate(x0, lag_time_ns=1.0)
save_frames(x_tau, Path("outputs/adk-endpoint"))
```

### Simulating Time-Ordered Trajectories
While standard propagation produces unordered bags of endpoints, `simulate_trajectory()` strings together rollouts into time-ordered trajectories where each frame builds upon the previous step:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "NaturalLanguageSpace"
        Start["InitialConformation"] --> Rollout["ParallelRollouts"]
        Rollout --> TimeSeries["TimeOrderedTrajectory"]
    end
    subgraph "CodeEntitySpace"
        S0["sample_equilibrium()"] --> Sim["simulate_trajectory()"]
        Sim --> Traj["mdtraj.Trajectory"]
    end
    Start -.-> S0
    Rollout -.-> Sim
    TimeSeries -.-> Traj

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:black,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 2: Workflow mapping from equilibrium sampling to time-ordered trajectory simulation.*

Using `simulate_trajectory()` from `examples/simulate_a_trajectory.py`:
```python
lag_time_ns = 50
num_trajectory_steps = 20
num_trajectories = 4

trajectories = simulate_trajectory(
    system,
    model=model,
    x0=x0[[0] * num_trajectories],
    lag_time_ns=lag_time_ns,
    num_trajectory_steps=num_trajectory_steps,
    seed=1,
)
```

Sources: `docs/propagation.md:90-119`, `examples/simulate_a_trajectory.py:37-76`

---

## External Starting Structures and Atom Mapping
When propagating from external CIF structures (such as those downloaded from the PDB), coordinates must be aligned with the system's expected atom order using `map_cif_atom_order()`:

```python
system = System.from_yaml("system.yaml")
x0 = map_cif_atom_order(system, "initial.cif")
emu = EmuSession(system, model=load_model(), mode="equilibrium")
endpoints = emu.propagate(x0, lag_time_ns=1.0)
save_frames(endpoints, Path("outputs/from-external-cif"))
```

- **Constraints**: The target file must provide coordinates for every chain, residue, and atom specified in the system definition. Missing atoms cannot be populated automatically during the propagation mapping stage.

Sources: `docs/propagation.md:120-149`

---

# Page: Structure and Chemistry Data Layer

# Structure and Chemistry Data Layer

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/system.md](docs/system.md)
- [src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml](src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml)

</details>



The Structure and Chemistry Data Layer manages molecular system definitions, sequence and alignment inputs, stereochemical restraints, and all-atom structure generation. It translates high-level domain concepts—such as proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, modified residues, and branched glycans—into tensor representations and coordinates suitable for the BioMoA score model stack.

For detailed technical implementations, refer to the child pages:
- [Structure Representation and Building](#5.1) (`src/bioemu2/structure`)
- [Data Interface and System Parsing](#5.2) (`src/bioemu2/data_interface`)
- [MSA Generation and Embedding Reuse](#5.3) (`src/bioemu2/msa`)

---

## 5.1. Structure Representation and Building

The structure subpackage (`src/bioemu2/structure`) is responsible for converting numerical model outputs and internal tokenized graphs back into physical, all-atom Cartesian coordinates and standard file formats like mmCIF and XTC. It manages polymer builders, rigid-body alignment, scatter operations, template parsing, and Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) bond and angle definitions.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        A["All-Atom Model Output"]
        B["Polymer Builder"]
        C["CIF and CCD Stereochemistry"]
    end
    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        D["src/bioemu2/structure/all_atom_structure.py"] --> E["src/bioemu2/structure/builder.py"]
        E --> F["src/bioemu2/structure/polymer_builder.py"]
        C --> G["src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml"]
    end
    A --> D
    B --> F
    
    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```

For comprehensive details on all-atom handling, scatter operations, reference structures, and CCD IO routines, see the child page [Structure Representation and Building](#5.1).

Sources: [`src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml:1-200`]().

---

## 5.2. Data Interface and System Parsing

The data interface module (`src/bioemu2/data_interface`) handles the parsing, validation, and conversion of molecular system configurations. Users define molecular systems programmatically via `System` classes or declarative YAML files [docs/system.md:1-23](). 

BioEmu2 supports proteins, RNA, DNA, ligands (via CCD code, SMILES, or InChI), modified residues, and branched molecules [docs/system.md:33-207](). It also provides a CLI converter for Boltz-format input files [docs/system.md:28-31]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        A["User YAML System Spec"]
        B["Boltz Input Converter"]
        C["Ligand and Modification Validator"]
    end
    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        D["src/bioemu2/data_interface/system.py"] --> E["src/bioemu2/data_interface/boltz.py"]
        D --> F["src/bioemu2/data_interface/ligand_validators.py"]
        F --> G["src/bioemu2/data_interface/bond_reference.py"]
    end
    A --> D
    B --> E
    C --> F
    
    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```

For full documentation on parsing schemas, bond references, hierarchy representations, and validation logic, see the child page [Data Interface and System Parsing](#5.2).

Sources: [`docs/system.md:1-100`]().

---

## 5.3. MSA Generation and Embedding Reuse

Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs) and template embeddings provide evolutionary context to the BioMoA models. The MSA subpackage (`src/bioemu2/msa`) manages sequence searching, ColabFold integration, alignment filtering, feature extraction, and embedding caching workflows. Reusing cached embeddings allows rapid iterative sampling and prevents redundant compute overhead during large batch screens.

For details on MSA parsing, feature extraction pipelines, and the embedding reuse workflow, see the child page [MSA Generation and Embedding Reuse](#5.3).

---

# Page: Structure Representation and Building

# Structure Representation and Building

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/bioemu2/assets/.gitignore](src/bioemu2/assets/.gitignore)
- [src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt](src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt)
- [src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml](src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

The `src/bioemu2/structure` subpackage and its associated assets provide the foundational data structures, geometry builders, and stereochemical dictionaries required to represent, construct, batch, and manipulate atomic-level biomolecular systems within BioEmu2. This layer bridges high-level molecular system definitions (such as sequences, PDB IDs, and YAML system specifications) with the tensor-based representations consumed by the BioMoA score model and denoising samplers. Key responsibilities include managing all-atom coordinate serialization, polymer chain building from sequence templates, batching variable-sized molecular graphs, scattering tensors across distributed ranks, and enforcing chemical component dictionary (CCD) stereochemistry.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["NaturalLanguage:SystemSpecification"] --> B["CodeEntity:polymer_builder.py"]
    B --> C["CodeEntity:AllAtomStructure"]
    C --> D["CodeEntity:batch.py"]
    D --> E["CodeEntity:score_model.py"]
    
    subgraph "Structure Subpackage"
        B
        C
        D
    end
  
    Sources: src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt:1-14, src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml:1-10
```

---

## All-Atom Representation and CCD Assets

Biomolecular structures are represented using persistent tensor-based data structures that encapsulate node features, coordinates, bond indices, bond types, formal charges, and element types. The fundamental class driving this representation is `AllAtomStructure`, which organizes atomic coordinates and stereochemical features [src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt:1-14]().

Template assets stored in PyTorch serialized formats provide baseline geometry for standard residues (such as amino acids ALA, ARG, ASN, etc.) [src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt:12-28](). Stereochemical constraints—including bond lengths and valence angles derived from OpenStructure and chemical component dictionaries—are maintained in YAML specifications [src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml:1-50]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["StereoChemistryYAML" / "src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml"] --> B["BondAndAngleConstraints"]
    C["PolymerTemplatesPT" / "src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt"] --> D["AllAtomStructure"]
    B --> D
    D --> E["TensorizedCoordinates"]
  
    Sources: src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt:1-28, src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml:1-50
```

- **`AllAtomStructure`**: Manages node counts, name encodings, element types, template coordinates, bond indices, bond types, and charges [src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt:1-28]().
- **Stereochemical Validation**: Ensures physical validity of bond angles, improper dihedrals, and equilibrium lengths during generation [src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml:6-50]().

Sources: `src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt:1-28`, `src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml:1-50`

---

## Polymer Builders and Template Matching

The polymer building pipeline translates molecular sequences into fully realized 3D atomic structures. 

- **`builder.py` & `polymer_builder.py`**: Handle chain-level construction, mapping sequence tokens to corresponding monomer templates retrieved from `polymer_templates.pt`. They allocate atom positions, construct backbone/side-chain atoms, and resolve missing coordinates.
- **`templates.py`**: Manages template retrieval and alignment logic, matching input sequences against known residue dictionaries and handling structural interpolations or profile-based template assignments.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Builder Pipeline"
        A["SequenceInput"] --> B["polymer_builder.py"]
        B --> C["templates.py"]
        C --> D["builder.py"]
        D --> E["AllAtomStructureInstance"]
    end
  
    Sources: src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt:1-14
```

Sources: `src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt:1-14`

---

## Batching and Scattering Utilities

Because biomolecules vary significantly in length and atom count, BioEmu2 implements custom batching and tensor restructuring operators.

- **`batch.py`**: Combines multiple `AllAtomStructure` instances or tensor dictionaries into unified batched structures, handling padding, masking, and index offset adjustments for bonds and nodes.
- **`scatter.py`**: Performs inverse operations, scattering batched representations back into individual structural units or distributing tensor slices across devices for context-parallel and data-parallel execution.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Batching Logic"
        A["IndividualStructures"] --> B["batch.py"]
        B --> C["BatchedTensorRepresentation"]
        C --> D["scatter.py"]
        D --> E["DistributedStructures"]
    end
  
    Sources: src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt:1-14
```

Sources: `src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt:1-14`

---

## Preparation and Reference Structures

Before structures are passed to the diffusion score model or physical steering potentials, they undergo preprocessing and alignment.

- **`preparation.py`**: Handles cleaning, protonation state assignment, atom ordering standardization, and coordinate sanitization of input PDB or CIF files.
- **`ref_struct.py`**: Defines reference structural states, ideal geometries, and alignment targets used during root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) calculations, rigid alignments, and loss computations.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Preparation Pipeline"
        A["RawPDBorCIF"] --> B["preparation.py"]
        B --> C["ref_struct.py"]
        C --> D["AlignedStandardStructure"]
    end
  
    Sources: src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml:1-20
```

Sources: `src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml:1-20`

---

## CIF IO and Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) Data

BioEmu2 includes robust input/output handlers for Crystallographic Information File (CIF) formats and Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) data. These modules parse residue topologies, bond connectivity tables, and stereochemical descriptors, ensuring that non-standard ligands, modified residues, and nucleic acids are accurately represented alongside standard proteins.

Sources: `src/bioemu2/assets/stereo_chemistry.yaml:1-10`, `src/bioemu2/assets/polymer_templates.pt:1-10`

# Page: Data Interface and System Parsing

# Data Interface and System Parsing

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/boltz.md](docs/boltz.md)
- [docs/system.md](docs/system.md)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
The data interface subsystem (`src/bioemu2/data_interface`) is responsible for defining, validating, serializing, and parsing molecular system specifications for BioEmu2 [docs/system.md:18-23](), [docs/boltz.md:3-8](). It bridges external file formats (such as Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 input YAMLs) and native Python data structures (`System`, `Protein`, `RNA`, `DNA`, `Ligand`, `Branched`, and `ModifiedResidue`) utilized across structure prediction, equilibrium sampling, and time propagation workflows [docs/system.md:18-104](), [docs/boltz.md:3-8]().

Sources: `docs/boltz.md:3-8`, `docs/system.md:18-23`

## 1. Molecular System Representation and Validation (`system.py`)
The `System` class defines the complete molecular composition passed to BioEmu2 [docs/system.md:18-23](). It encapsulates molecular entities, optional non-standard covalent bonds, and mappings from canonical chain IDs to author chain IDs [docs/system.md:18-23]().

- **Entity Types**: Systems support `Protein`, `RNA`, `DNA`, `Ligand`, and `Branched` entities [docs/system.md:86]().
- **Validation**: Upon initialization, `System` validates that canonical chain identifiers (`asym_ids`) are unique across the system and restricted to a maximum length of four characters [docs/system.md:60-62]().
- **Convenience Builders**: Systems can be instantiated directly or via `System.from_description()`, which assigns sequential chain IDs starting at `A` from lists of polymer sequences and ligand codes [docs/system.md:88-104]().
- **Modifications**: Modified or non-canonical residues are specified using `ModifiedResidue` objects containing a 1-based `res_id` and a chemical identifier (CCD code or InChI) [docs/system.md:112-121]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural_Language_Space"
        NL_Prot["Trp-cage Sequence 'NLYIQ...'"]
        NL_Lig["ATP Ligand Code 'ATP'"]
    end
    subgraph "Code_Entity_Space"
        CE_Prot["Protein(sequence=..., asym_ids=...)"]
        CE_Lig["Ligand(ccd_code=..., asym_ids=...)"]
        CE_Sys["System(entities=[...])"]
    end
    NL_Prot --> CE_Prot
    NL_Lig --> CE_Lig
    CE_Prot --> CE_Sys
    CE_Lig --> CE_Sys
```
*Figure 1: Mapping natural language molecular descriptions to BioEmu2 `Protein`, `Ligand`, and `System` code entities.*

Sources: `docs/system.md:18-136`

## 2. Boltz Format Conversion and Loading (`boltz.py`)
BioEmu2 provides conversion utilities to ingest external Boltz-format input files into native BioEmu2 system configurations [docs/boltz.md:3-8]().

- **Conversion CLI and API**: The `bioemu2 convert-boltz` command-line tool and the programmatic `convert_boltz()` function translate `version: 1` Boltz input YAMLs into BioEmu2 system YAMLs [docs/boltz.md:3-8](), [docs/boltz.md:73-83]().
- **Supported Fields**: The converter preserves polymer sequences, chain IDs, polymer modifications (`ModifiedResidue`), SMILES/CCD ligands, and covalent bond definitions [docs/boltz.md:108-118]().
- **Contact Constraints**: Contact constraints defined in Boltz inputs are extracted into contact tokens and loaded alongside the system via `load_system_and_contacts()` [docs/boltz.md:82-89](), [docs/boltz.md:117-118]().
- **Ignored Fields**: Per-chain MSA paths, template configurations, and affinity properties in Boltz files are explicitly ignored with warnings; alignments must be handled separately via `get_msa()` [docs/boltz.md:67-71](), [docs/boltz.md:131-139]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "External_Input_Space"
        Ext_File["Boltz_YAML_Input_File"]
    end
    subgraph "Code_Entity_Space"
        Code_Conv["convert_boltz()"]
        Code_Load["load_system_and_contacts()"]
        Code_Sys["System_Object"]
        Code_Cont["Contact_Conditioning"]
    end
    Ext_File --> Code_Conv
    Code_Conv --> Code_Load
    Code_Load --> Code_Sys
    Code_Load --> Code_Cont
```
*Figure 2: Data flow from external Boltz YAML files through `convert_boltz()` and `load_system_and_contacts()` into BioEmu2 system and contact structures.*

Sources: `docs/boltz.md:3-89`, `docs/boltz.md:108-141`
