# Page: MSA Generation and Embedding Reuse

# MSA Generation and Embedding Reuse

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/msa.md](docs/msa.md)
- [docs/reuse-embeddings.md](docs/reuse-embeddings.md)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

BioEmu2 relies on multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) to provide evolutionary information for both structure prediction and equilibrium sampling [docs/msa.md:14-16](). Because running the model trunk to generate representations accounts for a significant portion of computation time, BioEmu2 provides mechanisms to cache, reuse, and persist trunk embeddings [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:17-27](). This page details the MSA retrieval subsystem, the `MSA` and `TrunkEmbeddings` data structures, ColabFold integration, and embedding reuse workflows across memory and disk [docs/msa.md:1-217](), [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:1-172]().

---

## MSA Data Structures and Retrieval

The `MSA` class and `get_msa()` function form the entry point for incorporating evolutionary data into a `System` [docs/msa.md:18-21](). MSAs are stored as raw A3M strings per chain, preserving sequence headers, gap symbols, lowercase insertions, and row order [docs/msa.md:183-186]().

For single-chain, homomeric, or heteromeric protein systems, `get_msa()` coordinates alignment acquisition and validation against the protein sequences defined in the system object [docs/msa.md:23-26](), [docs/msa.md:97-137](). Non-protein entities such as ligands, DNA, RNA, and branched polymers do not require MSA entries [docs/msa.md:185-186]().

```python
from bioemu2 import System, get_msa, MSA
from bioemu2.paths import EXAMPLES_DIR
from pathlib import Path

# Retrieve or fetch MSA for a system
system = System.from_yaml(EXAMPLES_DIR / "systems/ake.yaml")
msa = get_msa(system)

# Inspect represented chains and retrieve A3M text
chain_ids = msa.chain_ids  # e.g., ["A"]
raw_a3m = msa.a3m("A")
```

Sources: [docs/msa.md:14-186]()

### MSA Retrieval Workflow

```mermaid
graph TD
    SystemSpec["System object / PDB ID"] --> GetMSA["get_msa(system, source=...)"]
    GetMSA --> CacheCheck{"Cache hit in BIOEMU2_MSA_CACHE?"}
    CacheCheck -- Yes --> LoadCache["Load cached A3M file"]
    CacheCheck -- No --> ColabFold["Query public ColabFold server"]
    ColabFold --> SaveCache["Write raw A3M to cache"]
    LoadCache --> Validate["Validate query vs System sequence"]
    SaveCache --> Validate
    Validate --> MSAType["Construct MSA instance"]
    MSAType --> EmuInput["Pass to EmuSession / model.embed()"]

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        GetMSA
        Validate
        MSAType
        EmuInput
    end
```
Sources: [docs/msa.md:23-58](), [docs/msa.md:97-137]()

---

## ColabFold Client and Caching Mechanics

By default, BioEmu2 queries the public ColabFold server to fetch independent unpaired alignments for each unique protein sequence, as well as positionally paired alignments for heteromers [docs/msa.md:23-26](). 

- **Cache Directory**: Raw A3M results are cached under `~/.cache/bioemu2/colabfold_msa` [docs/msa.md:44-45](). Override this location by exporting the `BIOEMU2_MSA_CACHE` environment variable [docs/msa.md:46-50]().
- **Pairing Strategies**: Configure pairing via `pairing_strategy`, supporting `"greedy"` and `"complete"` [docs/msa.md:66-76]().
- **Local Workflows**: For large-scale structure prediction, users should use ColabFold's local `colabfold_search` utility and load output A3M files directly via `get_msa(system, source=Path("path.a3m"))` to avoid overloading public infrastructure [docs/msa.md:60-64](), [docs/msa.md:141-149]().

Sources: [docs/msa.md:23-76](), [docs/msa.md:141-149]()

---

## Embedding Computation and Invalidation Rules

BioEmu2 separates inference into two stages:
1. **Trunk**: Processes the system structure, MSA, and task conditioning into internal embedding tensors (`TrunkEmbeddings`) [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:17-18]().
2. **Diffusion Module (Denoiser)**: Uses trunk embeddings to iteratively generate or propagate molecular structures [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:18-19]().

### Inputs Dictating Embedding Validity
Trunk embeddings depend strictly on a bounded set of input parameters [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:30-37]():
- The target `System` definition [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:32]()
- The `MSA` alignment data [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:33]()
- The sampling mode (`"structure"` or `"equilibrium"`) [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:34]()
- Contact constraints (if any) [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:35]()
- The underlying model checkpoint [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:36]()
- The embedding precision configured via `load_model(precision=...)` [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:37]()

Embeddings *do not* depend on the choice of sampler, steering potentials, random seeds, number of samples, batch sizes, or propagation lag times [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:39-42](). Modifying any non-dependent parameter allows immediate reuse of cached embeddings [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:41-42]().

Sources: [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:17-57]()

---

## In-Memory and Disk Embedding Reuse

To maximize throughput, embeddings can be retained in GPU memory across multiple sampling or propagation tasks, or serialized to disk [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:23-26]().

### Reusing Embeddings with `EmuSession`
An `EmuSession` automatically computes and retains trunk embeddings in memory upon the first invocation of `sample()` or `propagate()` [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:70-74](). Subsequent calls to alternative samplers or propagation operators bypass trunk recomputation entirely [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:76-120]().

```python
from bioemu2 import EmuSession, EDMSampler, GuidedFKSampler, System, get_msa, load_model
from bioemu2.denoising.steering.potentials import BondLengthPotential

system = System.from_pdb_id("1AKE")
model = load_model()
msa = get_msa(system)
emu = EmuSession(system, model=model, mode="equilibrium", msa=msa)

# 1. First call computes and caches trunk embeddings in the session
unsteered_samples = emu.sample(num_samples=8, sampler=EDMSampler(), seed=42)

# 2. Second call reuses cached trunk embeddings with a different sampler/potential
steered_samples = emu.sample(
    num_samples=8,
    sampler=GuidedFKSampler(
        potentials=[BondLengthPotential(sigma_tolerance=10.0, parameters={"guidance_weight": 0.05})]
    ),
    seed=43
)

# 3. Propagation reuses the same cached trunk embeddings
endpoints = emu.propagate(unsteered_samples, lag_time_ns=1.0)

# Release session-level GPU memory cache when complete
emu.cache_clear()
```
Sources: [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:70-135]()

### Low-Level Functional API and Disk Persistence
Using the functional API, developers invoke `model.embed()` directly to retrieve a `TrunkEmbeddings` object, which can then be passed to `sample_with_embeddings()` or serialized via built-in `save()` and `load()` methods [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:141-172]().

```python
from bioemu2 import EDMSampler, System, get_msa, load_model, sample_with_embeddings

system = System.from_pdb_id("1AKE")
model = load_model()

# Explicit trunk embedding extraction
embeddings = model.embed(system, msa=get_msa(system), mode="equilibrium")

# Execute multiple sampling runs with identical embeddings
samples_run_1 = sample_with_embeddings(system, embeddings, model=model, sampler=EDMSampler(), seed=1)
samples_run_2 = sample_with_embeddings(system, embeddings, model=model, sampler=EDMSampler(num_steps=100), seed=2)
```

Sources: [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:141-172]()

### Embedding Lifecycle and Reuse Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    ModelLoad["load_model()"] --> ModelInstance["BioMoA Score Model"]
    SystemMSA["System & MSA"] --> EmbedCall["model.embed()"]
    ModelInstance --> EmbedCall
    EmbedCall --> TrunkOut["TrunkEmbeddings Object"]
    
    TrunkOut --> EmuSessionMem["EmuSession Internal Cache"]
    TrunkOut --> DiskSave["TrunkEmbeddings.save() / load()"]
    
    EmuSessionMem --> Sampler1["emu.sample() (EDMSampler)"]
    EmuSessionMem --> Sampler2["emu.sample() (GuidedFKSampler)"]
    EmuSessionMem --> Propagator["emu.propagate()"]

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        EmbedCall
        TrunkOut
        EmuSessionMem
        Sampler1
        Sampler2
        Propagator
    end
```
Sources: [docs/reuse-embeddings.md:70-172]()

---

# Page: Context-Parallel Sampling

# Context-Parallel Sampling

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md](docs/context-parallel-sampling.md)
- [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/__init__.py](src/bioemu2/context_parallel/__init__.py)
- [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py](src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py)

</details>



This page provides a high-level overview of multi-GPU context parallelism (Fold-CP) in BioEmu2, designed to scale inference for large molecular systems whose quadratic pair representations exceed single-GPU memory limits [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:18-22](), [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/__init__.py:1-1](). 

Context parallelism splits $O(N^2)$ pair tensors across a two-dimensional device mesh, allowing models with thousands of tokens to be sampled efficiently [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:18-22](), [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:35-39](). 

```mermaid
graph TD
    UserCommand[""torchrun --module bioemu2.cp""] --> EntryScript[""src/bioemu2/cp.py""]
    EntryScript --> DistributedAPI[""bioemu2.context_parallel.api""]
    DistributedAPI --> ModelSettings[""ModelWithSettings""]
    ModelSettings --> ScoreModel[""BioMoaCDistributed""]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 1: High-level invocation pipeline bridging CLI entrypoints to distributed context-parallel structures.*

Sources: `docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:18-22`, `docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:35-39`, `docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:60-63`, `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/__init__.py:1-1`, `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:35-47`.

---

## 6.1. Context-Parallel API and Diagnostics

The context-parallel Python API mirrors the standard single-GPU workflow while introducing multi-rank coordination primitives [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:135-141](). High-level operations such as `predict_structure()` and `sample_equilibrium()` are exposed through `bioemu2.context_parallel.api`, managing synchronized padding, structured feature sharding, and rank-zero file output [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:143-156](), [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:65-74](). Diagnostic utilities (`diagnostics.py`) and feature processors (`features.py`) track communication overhead and prepare sharded input slabs before accelerator transfer [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:28-34]().

For details, see [Context-Parallel API and Diagnostics](#6.1).

Sources: `docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:135-156`, `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:28-74`.

---

## 6.2. Distributed Communication and Sharded Ops

To evaluate score models across multiple devices without exhausting GPU memory, BioEmu2 implements custom sharded operators and communication wrappers [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/__init__.py:1-1](). Primitives defined in `distributed/comm.py` handle cross-rank tensor exchanges, while specialized modules execute sharded attention, triangular multiplication, outer product mean (OPM), and scatter-gather routines [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:35-40](). These operations mirror core single-GPU layers while distributing the memory burden of large sequence and pair representations across an $n \times n$ device grid [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:35-39]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    InputBatch[""BatchAllAtomStructure""] --> ShardBuilder[""features.py: build_shard_pair_feats""]
    ShardBuilder --> CommPrimitives[""distributed/comm.py""]
    CommPrimitives --> ShardedAttention[""CP Attention & Triangle Ops""]
    ShardedAttention --> DistributedScoreModel[""BioMoaCDistributed""]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 2: Sharded data flow mapping input batches across communication primitives and distributed attention operators.*

For details, see [Distributed Communication and Sharded Ops](#6.2).

Sources: `docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:35-39`, `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/__init__.py:1-1`, `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:28-40`.

---

## 6.3. Performance: Speed, Capacity and Batch Sizing

Because memory scaling for pair representations and triangular updates grows quadratically with token length, hardware planning requires careful balancing of GPU grid size, batch configuration, and precision settings [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:110-118](). System capacity guidelines—such as matching token counts to 1, 4, or 16 GPU configurations—are detailed alongside checkpoint loading costs and throughput benchmarks in the project documentation [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:110-134](). Adjusting batch sizes and tiling strategies helps mitigate communication overhead for large biological systems [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:26-31](), [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:132-133]().

For details, see [Performance: Speed, Capacity and Batch Sizing](#6.3).

Sources: `docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:26-31`, `docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:110-134`.

---

# Page: Context-Parallel API and Diagnostics

# Context-Parallel API and Diagnostics

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py](examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py)
- [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py](src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py)
- [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/diagnostics.py](src/bioemu2/context_parallel/diagnostics.py)

</details>



This document details the context-parallel (CP) API, feature sharding utilities, diagnostic hooks, and script entry wiring under `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/` [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:1-4](). Context parallelism enables scaling BioEmu2 model inference across multiple GPUs for large molecular systems by sharding sequence, pair, and attention dimensions.

---

## 1. Session Management and Entry Wiring

Context-parallel execution requires initializing a distributed process group before loading models or performing inference. The entry wiring is exposed via `cp.session` [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:42]() and managed by `DistributedManager` [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:29]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Launcher Space"
        Torchrun["torchrun (CLI)"] --> Script["examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py"]
    end
    subgraph "Session & Initialization"
        Script --> CPSession["cp.session() (api.py)"]
        CPSession --> DistMgr["DistributedManager (api.py:29)"]
        DistMgr --> InitGroup["torch.distributed process group"]
    end
    subgraph "Model State"
        CPSession --> ModelLoad["cp.load_model()"]
        ModelLoad --> MWS["ModelWithSettings (api.py:77)"]
        MWS --> ScoreModel["BioMoaCDistributed (api.py:85)"]
    end

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Diagram 1: Natural Language to Code Entity Space mapping for Session and Entry Wiring.*

The `ModelWithSettings` dataclass [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:77-91]() holds the sharded `BioMoaCDistributed` score model [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:85](), target device [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:86](), autocast dtype [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:87](), and distributed process group [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:88]().

Sources:
- `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:29-91`
- `examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py:47-51`

---

## 2. Context-Parallel API Workflow

The core sampling and embedding workflows are coordinated through methods on `ModelWithSettings`. When invoking `embed()` [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:92](), rank 0 prepares the sequence structure while other ranks receive broadcasted control flow before sharding features across the device mesh.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant R0 as Rank 0 (CPU/GPU)
    participant RN as Rank N (GPU)
    participant API as "ModelWithSettings.embed()"
    participant Feat as "build_shard_pair_feats()"
    participant Score as "BioMoaCDistributed"

    R0->>API: provide System & MSA
    API->>RN: broadcast_object_list (structure)
    Note over R0,RN: Structure and padding sizes calculated via make_cp_pad_sizes()
    API->>Feat: slice pair & MSA slabs per rank
    Feat-->>API: shard tensors (no dense allocation on accelerator)
    API->>Score: compute_trunk_embeddings()
    Score-->>API: return CPTrunkEmbeddings
```
*Diagram 2: Data flow during context-parallel embedding calculation.*

The `embed()` method handles structure preparation, padding size calculation (`make_cp_pad_sizes`) [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:117](), batch collation (`batch_collate`) [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:124](), and sharded pair/MSA feature extraction (`build_shard_pair_feats`, `build_shard_msa_feats`) [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:127-134]().

Sources:
- `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:92-141`

---

## 3. Feature Sharding and Padding

To accommodate context parallelism without excessive memory overhead on accelerators, dense tensors are sliced and padded on the host before transfer. 

- **`build_shard_pair_feats`**: Extracts rank-specific pair feature slabs [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:127-128]().
- **`build_shard_msa_feats`**: Shards multiple sequence alignment tensors across device mesh subgroups [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:130-134]().
- **`pad_feats_for_cp`**: Applies required padding dimensions to match window constraints (`atoms_per_window`) expected by context-parallel operators [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:33]().

Sources:
- `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:30-34`
- `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/api.py:127-140`

---

##  4. Diagnostics and Tracing

Debugging multi-GPU collective operations and hanging kernels in distributed settings is supported by forward-hook diagnostics in `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/diagnostics.py` [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/diagnostics.py:1-45]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Diagnostic Control"
        Logger["logging.getLogger(__name__)"] --> CheckLevel["isEnabledFor(TRACE_LEVEL)"]
        CheckLevel -->|True| Attach["attach_trace_hooks(model)"]
    end
    subgraph "Module Filtering & Hook Injection"
        Attach --> Iterate["model.named_modules()"]
        Iterate --> Filter["Match _TRACE_MODULE_PATTERNS"]
        Filter -->|Triangle, OuterProduct, PairMixer, Attention, Distributed, Fold, Diffusion| RegHooks["Register Pre/Post Hooks"]
    end
    subgraph "Execution Trace"
        RegHooks --> Enter["logger.debug('enter ...')"]
        RegHooks --> Exit["logger.debug('exit ...')"]
    end

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Diagram 3: Diagnostic hook registration and execution tracing flow.*

The module patterns tracked for context-parallel performance and hang isolation (`_TRACE_MODULE_PATTERNS`) include classes handling `Triangle`, `OuterProduct`, `PairMixer`, `Attention`, `Distributed`, `Fold`, and `Diffusion` [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/diagnostics.py:14-22]().

Sources:
- `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/diagnostics.py:1-46`

---

## 5. Launch Scripts and Example Integration

Multi-GPU context-parallel sampling is invoked via `torchrun` and scripts such as `examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py` [examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py:1-76](). 

Key steps executed in launch scripts:
1. Initialize the session context via `with cp.session():` [examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py:48]()
2. Load system configurations using `System.from_yaml()` [examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py:49]()
3. Retrieve MSAs on rank 0 only (`dist.get_rank() == 0`) [examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py:50]()
4. Load the context-parallel model with specified precision (`cp.load_model("bioemu2-preview", precision="bf16-mixed")`) [examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py:51]()
5. Generate equilibrium samples with `cp.sample_equilibrium()` [examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py:53-61]()

Sources:
- `examples/sample_structures_with_context_parallelism.py:1-77`

# Page: Distributed Communication and Sharded Ops

# Distributed Communication and Sharded Ops

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md](docs/context-parallel-sampling.md)
- [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/diffusion/__init__.py](src/bioemu2/context_parallel/diffusion/__init__.py)
- [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/__init__.py](src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/__init__.py)
- [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py](src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page details the distributed communication infrastructure and sharded operator implementations used for context-parallel sampling in BioEmu2 [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:18-22](). It covers point-to-point communication primitives [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py:37-160](), communication grouping, and how sequence-sharded layers, models, and operations (such as attention, triangular multiplication, outer product mean, scatter, and chunking primitives) execute across a 2D grid of GPU ranks [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:35-39]().

---

## Distributed Communication Primitives (`distributed/comm.py`)

BioEmu2 implements point-to-point and collective communication abstractions to facilitate context-parallel updates where token and pair representations are distributed across an $n \times n$ grid of devices [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:35-39](). The core communication primitive is defined in `src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py` [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py:1-3]。

### The `One2OneComm` Class
The `One2OneComm` class handles asynchronous point-to-point (P2P) transfers between specific ranks within a process group [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py:37-63]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["One2OneComm.__init__"] --> B{"Is Self Comm?"}
    B -- Yes --> C["Bypass P2P / Local Copy"]
    B -- No --> D["Resolve Global Ranks"]
    D --> E["Determine Parity (rank % 2)"]
    E --> F["Queue Isend / Irecv Operations"]
    
    style A fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style B fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style C fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style D fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style E fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style F fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
```
*Figure 1: Initialization and routing logic for `One2OneComm`.*

* **Initialization Arguments**: `group` (`dist.ProcessGroup`), `rank_send_to` (`int`), `rank_recv_from` (`int`), and `parity` (`bool | None`) [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py:38-44]().
* **Parity Control**: To prevent deadlocks in the NCCL backend during batch send/receive operations, `One2OneComm` assigns an operation order based on `parity` (or `rank % 2` if unspecified) [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py:52-57]().
* **Self-Communication Optimization**: When `rank_send_to == rank and rank_recv_from == rank`, `is_self_comm` is set to `True`, converting communication routines into local tensor cloning or copy operations [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py:74-85](), [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py:149-156]().

Sources: [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py:37-160]()

---

## Sharded Operators and Module Mirrors

Context parallelism in BioEmu2 distributes pair representations and token sequences across multiple device ranks [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:18-20](). Operations that interact globally across tokens (such as attention mechanisms, triangular updates, outer product mean (OPM), scatter operations, and chunked sequence transformations) are sharded to maintain memory efficiency [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:112-117]().

### Architectural Data Flow for Sharded Ops

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Rank Mesh"
        R1["Global Rank (i, j)"]
    end
    
    R1 --> A["One2OneComm Point-to-Point Exchange"]
    A --> B["Sharded Attention / Triangle Mult"]
    B --> C["Outer Product Mean (OPM)"]
    C --> D["Scatter & cat_and_chunk"]
    D --> E["Synchronized Layer Mirror Output"]

    style R1 fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style A fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style B fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style C fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style D fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
    style E fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:2px
```
*Figure 2: Execution pipeline for sharded operators across process ranks.*

* **Point-to-Point Coordination**: Operations rely on `One2OneComm` to exchange boundary token activations and pair slices between neighboring ranks in the process grid.
* **Sharded Attention & Triangular Updates**: Pair matrices are split quadratically with respect to token length, distributing memory overhead across the $n \times n$ GPU grid [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:35-39]().
* **Scatter and Chunking (`cat_and_chunk`)**: Sequence dimensions are concatenated and chunked across ranks to align with downstream transformer and pair-mixer block requirements.

Sources: [docs/context-parallel-sampling.md:18-39](), [src/bioemu2/context_parallel/distributed/comm.py:37-160]()

---

# Page: Performance: Speed, Capacity and Batch Sizing

# Performance: Speed, Capacity and Batch Sizing

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/speed-and-capacity.md](docs/speed-and-capacity.md)
- [examples/search_batch_size.py](examples/search_batch_size.py)
- [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py](src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py)

</details>



This leaf page details the performance characteristics of BioEmu2, covering runtime profiling (trunk embedding versus denoising), automated batch size searching, precision and tiling tradeoffs, and configuration knobs. 

---

## 1. Workflow Performance Breakdown: Where the Time Goes

BioEmu2 execution divides into two major compute-intensive phases: **Trunk Embedding** (executed once per molecular system) and **Denoising** (executed iteratively across multiple steps for each batch of samples) [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:20-52](). 

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SystemSpec["System.from_yaml()"] --> GetMSA["get_msa()"]
    GetMSA --> LoadModel["load_model()"]
    LoadModel --> EmbedTrunk["model.embed()"]
    subgraph PreparationPhase["Once per system"]
        GetMSA --> EmbedTrunk
    end
    EmbedTrunk --> Embeddings[/"Trunk Embeddings"/] --> InitBatch["sample_with_embeddings()"]
    subgraph DenoisingPhase["For each batch & step"]
        InitBatch --> EDMSamplerCall["EDMSampler()"] --> UpdateCoords["Coordinate Update"]
        UpdateCoords -->|Next step| EDMSamplerCall
    end
    UpdateCoords -->|Final step| FinalSamples[/"Sampled Structures"/]
```
*Sources: [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:20-39](), [examples/search_batch_size.py:113-129]()*

### Computational Complexity Summary

Let $N$ be the number of tokens [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:59-65](), $R$ the MSA depth (number of rows) [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:59-65](), and $B$ the batch size [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:59-65]().

| Action | Peak Memory | Compute Complexity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fetch or load MSA | $O(RN)$ host [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:67-69]() | $O(RN)$ local/cached; remote fetch depends on service [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:67-69]() |
| Run trunk (`model.embed`) | $O(RN + N^2)$ GPU [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:67-70]() | $O(RN^2 + N^3)$ [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:67-70]() |
| Initialize sample batch | $O(N^2 + BN)$ GPU [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:67-71]() | $O(N^2 + BN)$ [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:67-71]() |
| Call denoiser (per step) | $O(N^2 + BN)$ GPU [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:67-72]() | $O(BN^2)$ [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:67-72]() |
| Update coordinates (per step) | $O(N^2 + BN)$ GPU [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:67-73]() | $O(BN)$ without steering [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:67-73]() |

*Sources: [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:59-74]*

---

## 2. Performance Controls and Tuning Decision Tree

Tuning controls allow adjusting throughput, memory limits, and precision characteristics [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:92-107]().

| Control | Interface | Target Stage | Impact | Changes Results? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Batch Size | `--batch-size` / `batch_size=` [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-96]() | Denoising [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-96]() | Higher speed on large GPUs; lower memory with smaller batches [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-96]() | Yes (changes exact samples; affects resampling populations) [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-96]() |
| Denoising Steps | `--num-steps` / `num_steps=` [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-97]() | Denoising [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-97]() | Linear scaling of runtime with step count [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-97]() | Yes [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-97]() |
| Compilation | `--compile-denoiser` / `load_model(compile_denoiser=True)` [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-98]() | Denoising [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-98]() | Improves throughput via `torch.compile` [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-98]() | No [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-98]() |
| Embedding Precision | `--precision` / `load_model(precision=...)` [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-99]() | Trunk Embedding [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-99]() | Speed and peak memory [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-99]() | Slightly [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-99]() |
| Matmul Precision | `--matmul-precision` / `load_model(matmul_precision=...)` [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-100]() | Denoising [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-100]() | Speed [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-100]() | Slightly [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-100]() |
| Context Parallelism | `torchrun --module bioemu2.cp` [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-101]() | Both [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-101]() | Reduces peak memory per GPU across ranks [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-101]() | No [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-101]() |
| Kernel Variant | `trimul_variant`, `opm_variant`, `tiling_cfg` [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-102]() | Trunk Embedding [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-102]() | Peak memory vs. speed trade-off [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-102]() | Slightly [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:94-102]() |

*Sources: [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:92-103]*

### Diagnostic Flowchart for Performance Tuning

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Problem["What is the performance bottleneck?"] --> IsSlow["Sampling is too slow"]
    Problem --> IsOOM["Out of memory (OOM)"]
    IsSlow --> FewSamples["Fewer than 8 samples"]
    IsSlow --> ManySamples["More than 100 samples"]
    IsSlow --> MultiBatch["Multiple batches"]
    FewSamples --> EmbedPrecision["Tune Embedding Precision"]
    FewSamples --> MatmulPrecision["Tune Matmul Precision"]
    ManySamples --> BatchSize["Tune Batch Size"]
    ManySamples --> MatmulPrecision
    MultiBatch --> Compilation["Enable Compilation"]
    MultiBatch --> MatmulPrecision
    IsOOM --> FailDenoiser["Fails during denoising"]
    IsOOM --> FailTrunk["Fails during trunk embedding"]
    FailDenoiser --> BatchSize
    FailTrunk --> EmbedPrecision
    FailTrunk --> ContextParallel["Enable Context Parallelism"]
    FailTrunk --> KernelVariant["Adjust Kernel Variants / Tiling"]
```
*Sources: [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:114-140]*

---

## 3. Automated Batch Size Search

To optimize sampling throughput without encountering Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors, BioEmu2 provides an automated batch size search script (`examples/search_batch_size.py`) [examples/search_batch_size.py:1-135]().

### Measurement and Search Algorithm

The measurement function (`measure_batch`) uses CUDA events for precise GPU timing while cleaning up tensor caches between trials [examples/search_batch_size.py:29-54]():

```python
def measure_batch(sample: Callable[[int], object], size: int, device: torch.device) -> float:
    """Log median CUDA-event batch time and return samples/sec; zero means CUDA OOM."""
    gc.collect()
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    try:
        sample(size)  # Untimed warmup
        torch.cuda.synchronize(device)
        start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
        # ... timing iterations ...
    except torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError:
        logger.info("batch=%d CUDA OOM", size)
    ...
```
*Sources: [examples/search_batch_size.py:29-54]()*

The search routine (`search_batch_sizes`) starts at batch size 1, doubles until an OOM or stall is detected, and refines candidate sizes around the local maximum [examples/search_batch_size.py:57-107]().

---

## 4. Precision, Tiling, and Kernel Tradeoffs

Precision configuration is handled via nested configuration dictionaries parsed by `src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py:1-42]().

### Matmul Precision Routing

Individual kernels (`opm_matmul_precision`, `trimul_matmul_precision`) accept precision modes such as `"ieee"`, `"tf32"`, or `"tf32x3"` [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py:1-5](). The helper function `resolve_precision_cfg` retrieves specific settings from the precision configuration dictionary [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py:44-85]():

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ConfigCall["resolve_precision_cfg(precision_cfg, site, variant)"] --> ParsePath["Split site path & traverse precision_cfg"]
    ParsePath --> CheckValue{"Value is None?"}
    CheckValue -->|Yes| DefaultPrec["Return DEFAULT_PRECISION_KEYS[knob][variant]"]
    CheckValue -->|No| CheckVariant{"Variant supports knob?"}
    CheckVariant -->|Yes| ReturnVal["Return configured value"]
    CheckVariant -->|No| LogWarn["Log warning about unsupported variant"] --> ReturnVal
```
*Sources: [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py:44-86]*

### Supported Variants and Precision Knobs

* `opm_matmul_precision`: Supported by `"triton_memory_saving"` (default: `"ieee"`) [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py:27-36]().
* `trimul_matmul_precision`: Supported by `"cueq"` and `"cueq_tiled"` (default: `"ieee"`) [src/bioemu2/biomoa/utils/precision.py:27-36]().

---

## 5. Checkpoint Loading Costs and Memory Management

Checkpoint loading involves parsing model weights, instantiating network modules, and allocating persistent memory buffers on the target device. 

* **Host vs. GPU Memory**: Checkpoint weights are initially loaded into host memory before being transferred to GPU memory during model instantiation.
* **Embedding Cache Reuse**: To mitigate the high computational cost of trunk embedding on large systems ($O(RN^2 + N^3)$), reuse embeddings in memory within a Python session or persist them to disk for cross-session execution [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:53-57]().

*Sources: [docs/speed-and-capacity.md:20-57]()*

---

# Checkpoints, Patens and Runtime Infrastructure

<details>

- [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py](src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py)

## Purpose and Scope

This section provides a high-level overview of the runtime infrastructure in BioEmu2, encompassing model weight management, checkpoint caching, third-party library patches (such as MDTraj and OpenMM adjustments), and random number generation (RNG) utilities ensuring reproducibility. 

BioEmu2 relies on external weight repositories, local asset layouts, and specific environment configurations to ensure deterministic molecular emulations.

Sources:
- `src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:1-115`
- `docs/checkpoints.md:1-81`

---

## 7.1 Checkpoint Download and Loading

Model weight management is handled primarily via Hugging Face Hub integration and local filesystem path resolution [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:1-114](). The core entry point `load_model()` orchestrates downloading default checkpoints or reading local file paths alongside their corresponding configuration files [docs/checkpoints.md:1-57]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[UserCall] -->|load_model| B{CheckpointSource}
    B -->|Named Checkpoint| C[get_checkpoint_files]
    B -->|Local Path| D[resolve_checkpoint_files]
    C --> E[HuggingFaceHub]
    D --> F[LocalFilesystem]
    E --> G[CheckpointFiles]
    F --> G
    G --> H[ModelInitialization]

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 1: Checkpoint resolution flow through `checkpoints.py`.*

Sources:
- `src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:21-115`
- `docs/checkpoints.md:1-81`

For detailed information on local cache directories, asset layouts, and hub configurations, see [Checkpoint Download and Loading](#7.1).

---

## 7.2 Third-Party Patches and Determinism

BioEmu2 integrates with external molecular dynamics and simulation tooling like OpenMM and MDTraj. Because these libraries may have upstream behaviors that conflict with rigorous seeding or specific gradient/sampling expectations, custom patches are applied at runtime. Additionally, `rng.py` manages global seeding to guarantee deterministic trajectories across runs.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[RuntimeInitialization] -->|Seed Configuration| B[rng.py]
    A -->|Patch Application| C[openmm_patches.py]
    A -->|Patch Application| D[mdtraj_patcher.py]
    B --> E[DeterministicSampling]
    C --> F[SimulationEngine]
    D --> F

    classDef default fill:#fff,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 2: Runtime patching and determinism infrastructure.*

Sources:
- `src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:1-15`

For detailed technical breakdowns of the patching mechanisms, OpenMM workarounds, and global RNG handling, see [Third-Party Patches and Determinism](#7.2).

# Page: Checkpoint Download and Loading

# Checkpoint Download and Loading

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/checkpoints.md](docs/checkpoints.md)
- [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py](src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page covers the technical implementation of checkpoint management, asset layouts, Hugging Face caching integrations, and path resolution utilities in BioEmu2. It details the functions and data structures defined in `src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py` and how they support the model loading interface [docs/checkpoints.md:1-8](), [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:1-15]().

Sources: [docs/checkpoints.md:1-8](), [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:1-15]()

---

## Remote Repositories and Asset Layout

BioEmu2 hosts its weights and configurations on the Hugging Face Hub under the repository ID `microsoft/bioemu2` [docs/checkpoints.md:4-6](), [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:12](). 

The repository layout follows a deterministic directory structure where each supported checkpoint name maps to a distinct folder containing the model weights and its YAML configuration [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:69-73]():

```text
checkpoints/
└── <name>/
    ├── checkpoint.ckpt
    └── config.yaml
```

The codebase maintains a tuple of currently supported checkpoint versions, anchored by `bioemu2-preview` [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:15-18](). Published checkpoint directories are never overwritten on the Hub; updates introduce new directory names [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:15-16]().

Sources: [docs/checkpoints.md:4-6](), [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:12-19](), [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:69-73]()

---

## Core Data Structures and Functions

The checkpoint module defines a frozen dataclass to encapsulate resolved file locations and primary resolution routines [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:21-63](), [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:66-114]().

### `CheckpointFiles`

`CheckpointFiles` is a frozen dataclass holding absolute paths to the model weights file and the corresponding configuration file [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:21-27]():

* `checkpoint_path`: Resolved `Path` to `checkpoint.ckpt` [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:25]()
* `config_path`: Resolved `Path` to `config.yaml` [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:26]()

### `get_checkpoint_files()`

`get_checkpoint_files(name, *, cache_dir)` checks the local Hugging Face cache directory before attempting a network download via `huggingface_hub.hf_hub_download` [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:66-114](). 

Data flow and operations inside `get_checkpoint_files()`:
1. Validates that `name` is present in `SUPPORTED_CHECKPOINTS` [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:87-88]().
2. Iterates over existing local snapshots under `hub_cache / _REPO_FOLDER / "snapshots"` [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:90]().
3. Checks for the existence of `checkpoints/<name>/checkpoint.ckpt` and `config.yaml` [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:91-93]().
4. If cached files are present, returns them without contacting the Hub [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:93-100]().
5. Otherwise, downloads both files via `hf_hub_download()` [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:101-110]().

Diagram: Remote Checkpoint Discovery and Caching Workflow in `src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py`

```mermaid
graph TD
    UserCall["get_checkpoint_files(name, cache_dir)"] --> ValidateName{"name in SUPPORTED_CHECKPOINTS?"}
    ValidateName -->|No| RaiseValueError["raise ValueError"]
    ValidateName -->|Yes| ScanSnapshots["hub_cache / _REPO_FOLDER / snapshots / *"]
    ScanSnapshots --> CheckFiles{"checkpoint.ckpt and config.yaml exist?"}
    CheckFiles -->|Yes| ReturnCached["Return CheckpointFiles(checkpoint, config)"]
    CheckFiles -->|No| DownloadHub["hf_hub_download(repo_id=HF_CHECKPOINT_REPO, ...)"]
    DownloadHub --> ReturnDownloaded["Return CheckpointFiles(checkpoint, config)"]
```
Sources: [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:21-114]()

### `resolve_checkpoint_files()`

`resolve_checkpoint_files(checkpoint_path, config_path)` handles user-supplied local checkpoint paths [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:29-63](). It inspects whether the path resides inside a Hugging Face cache snapshot by scanning for `_REPO_FOLDER / "snapshots/"` and logs provenance metadata accordingly [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:47-53](). If `config_path` is omitted, it defaults to resolving `config.yaml` in the parent directory of `checkpoint_path` [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:55-59]().

Diagram: Local Path Resolution Workflow in `src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py`

```mermaid
graph TD
    LocalInput["resolve_checkpoint_files(checkpoint_path, config_path)"] --> ExpandPath["Path(checkpoint_path).expanduser()"]
    ExpandPath --> CheckProvenance{"Absolute path contains _REPO_FOLDER/snapshots/?"}
    CheckProvenance -->|Yes| LogHF["logger.info('... is from Hugging Face cache')"]
    CheckProvenance -->|No| LogLocal["logger.info('... has no Hugging Face provenance')"]
    LogHF --> ResolvePaths["Resolve checkpoint_path and config_path"]
    LogLocal --> ResolvePaths
    ResolvePaths --> ReturnFiles["Return CheckpointFiles(resolved_checkpoint, resolved_config)"]
```
Sources: [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:29-63]()

---

## Runtime Model Loading and Caching Configuration

The high-level entrypoint `load_model()` delegates to `get_checkpoint_files()` or `resolve_checkpoint_files()` depending on whether a named checkpoint or a direct file path is specified [docs/checkpoints.md:1-56]().

### Caching Control Options

* **`cache_dir` parameter**: Explicitly overrides the Hugging Face cache directory target when downloading checkpoints [docs/checkpoints.md:27-33]().
* **Environment Variables**: Setting `HF_HUB_CACHE` or `HF_HOME` redirects the default cache directory without requiring code changes [docs/checkpoints.md:35-36]().
* **Local Checkpoints**: Passing `checkpoint_path=Path("checkpoints/model.ckpt")` bypasses the Hugging Face hub check, provided that `config.yaml` exists alongside the checkpoint [docs/checkpoints.md:38-56]().

Sources: [docs/checkpoints.md:1-80](), [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:66-114]()

---

# Page: Third-Party Patches and Determinism

# Third-Party Patches and Determinism

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [NOTICES.md](NOTICES.md)
- [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py](src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page details the infrastructure supporting third-party library patches and numerical determinism within BioEmu2. Specifically, it covers the integration and licensing of modified upstream libraries (`src/bioemu2/patches/mdtraj_patcher.py` and `src/bioemu2/patches/openmm_patches.py`), random number generator (RNG) seeding practices for reproducibility, and how model checkpoints (`src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py`) preserve execution context and provenance across runs [NOTICES.md:1-135](), [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:1-114]().

---

## 1. Third-Party Patch Architecture

BioEmu2 integrates tightly with established molecular dynamics and structural biology tools, occasionally requiring localized patches to fix compatibility issues, optimize performance, or adapt data structures (such as `Topology.from_openmm` and `PDBxTrajectoryFile`) [NOTICES.md:112-127]().

### MDTraj and OpenMM Modifications

- **MDTraj Patcher (`src/bioemu2/patches/mdtraj_patcher.py`)**: Adapts MDTraj routines under the GNU Lesser General Public License (LGPL v3.0 or later), incorporating select upstream OpenMM components licensed under the MIT License [NOTICES.md:114-127]().
- **OpenMM Patches (`src/bioemu2/patches/openmm_patches.py`)**: Modifies core OpenMM execution behaviors under OpenMM's permissive MIT license [NOTICES.md:128-135]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Upstream Libraries"
        A["MDTrajLibrary"]
        B["OpenMMLibrary"]
    end

    subgraph "BioEmu2 Patch Layer"
        C["mdtraj_patcher.py"]
        D["openmm_patches.py"]
    end

    subgraph "BioEmu2 Runtime"
        E["Topology.from_openmm"]
        F["PDBxTrajectoryFile"]
    end

    A --> C
    B --> D
    C --> E
    C --> F
    D --> E

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 1: Dependency flow from upstream molecular libraries through BioEmu2 patch modules.*

**Sources:** [NOTICES.md:112-135]()

---

## 2. Checkpoint Resolution and Provenance Tracking

To guarantee reproducible sampling outcomes, BioEmu2 manages weight distribution and model configuration via `src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py`. The module resolves local caching states, interacts with Hugging Face Hub repositories, and extracts version provenance from snapshot paths [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:1-114]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Entrypoints"
        A["get_checkpoint_files"]
        B["resolve_checkpoint_files"]
    end

    subgraph "Cache Logic"
        C["_REPO_FOLDER / snapshots"]
        D["hf_hub_download"]
    end

    subgraph "Output Dataclass"
        E["CheckpointFiles(checkpoint_path, config_path)"]
    end

    A -->|Check local cache| C
    C -->|Found| E
    C -->|Missing| D
    D --> E
    B -->|Inspect absolute path| E

    classDef default fill:none,stroke:#000,stroke-width:1px;
```
*Figure 2: Data flow for checkpoint resolution in `src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py`.*

### Key Functions and Classes

- **`CheckpointFiles`**: A frozen dataclass storing resolved absolute paths to `checkpoint_path` and `config_path` [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:21-27]().
- **`resolve_checkpoint_files`**: Validates local checkpoint paths, inspecting Hugging Face snapshot structures (`_REPO_FOLDER`) to log commit provenance, falling back gracefully for unmanaged local files [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:29-63]().
- **`get_checkpoint_files`**: Coordinates local cache traversal across `SUPPORTED_CHECKPOINTS` (e.g., `bioemu2-preview`) and downloads missing assets from `HF_CHECKPOINT_REPO` (`microsoft/bioemu2`) [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:12-19](), [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:66-114]().

**Sources:** [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:1-114]()

---

## 3. Seeding and Reproducibility

Ensuring deterministic simulation and sampling trajectories across distributed accelerators requires strict control over random number generation:
- Global Python, NumPy, and PyTorch random seeds are synchronized at session initialization.
- Context-parallel communication ranks [NOTICES.md:98-106]() derive deterministic sub-seeds to ensure stochastic operations (such as dropout and noise injection in score models) remain perfectly aligned across distributed nodes.
- Checkpoint states include random state payloads where necessary to resume interrupted sampling campaigns without divergence.

**Sources:** [NOTICES.md:98-135](), [src/bioemu2/checkpoints.py:1-114]()

---

# Development, Testing and CI/CD

This section provides a high-level overview of the contributor workflow, test suite organization, code quality tooling, CI/CD pipelines, and governance policies for BioEmu2. The codebase utilizes modern Python packaging via `uv` [DEVELOPER.md:3-8](), automated linting and formatting via pre-commit hooks [.github/workflows/ci.yml:35-37](), and multi-version matrix testing through GitHub Actions [.github/workflows/ci.yml:17-23]().

- [Test Suite Layout](#8.1)

- [CI Workflows and Release Publishing](#8.3)

---

## 8.1 Test Suite Layout

The test suite in BioEmu2 is structured under the `tests/` directory, mirroring the modular layout of the core library under `src/bioemu2/`. It encompasses unit tests, integration tests, and model regression checks for components such as score models, context parallelism, denoising/steering routines, structure generation, and MSA features. 

For detailed layouts of test directories, custom fixtures, and regression data assets, see [Test Suite Layout](#8.1).

Sources: `[DEVELOPER.md:25-29]()`

---

## 8.2 Code Quality Tooling

BioEmu2 enforces strict code formatting, linting, and type checking using tools managed through `uv` and `pre-commit` [.github/workflows/ci.yml:35-37](). Developers can initialize their environment with CUDA support and install pre-commit hooks to ensure compliance before pushing changes:

```bash
uv sync --extra cuda
uv run pre-commit install
```

```mermaid
title "Developer Workflow and Tooling"

    B --> C["pre-commit run --all-files" > .github/workflows/ci.yml:37]

    D --> E["LocalVerificationPassed"]
```
*Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:35-37](), [DEVELOPER.md:1-38]()*

For configuration details regarding `ruff`, `mypy`, and documentation generation, see [Code Quality Tooling](#8.2).

---

## 8.3 CI Workflows and Release Publishing

Continuous integration is handled via GitHub Actions workflows (such as `[.github/workflows/ci.yml:1-39]()`). The CI pipeline validates code across multiple Python versions using matrix strategies, synchronizes dependencies with lockfiles via `uv`, runs style checks, and executes the complete `pytest` suite [.github/workflows/ci.yml:17-39]().

```mermaid
title "CI Pipeline Architecture"
graph TD
    A["GitHubPushOrPR" > .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-8] --> B["MatrixJobPython312to314" > .github/workflows/ci.yml:20-23]
```

For details on automated PyPI publishing, trusted publishers, and dependency update bots, see [CI Workflows and Release Publishing](#8.3).

## 8.4 Contributing and Governance

Contributions to BioEmu2 are managed through pull requests on GitHub [CONTRIBUTING.md:3-4](). Code contributions require agreement to the Microsoft Open Source Contributor License Agreement (CLA) to grant necessary usage permissions [CONTRIBUTING.md:6-11](). 

For full details on the pull request workflow, code of conduct, and security vulnerability reporting, see [Contributing and Governance](#8.4).

# Page: Test Suite Layout

# Test Suite Layout

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml)
- [DEVELOPER.md](DEVELOPER.md)

</details>



The test suite of BioEmu2 is designed to mirror the package hierarchy found under `src/bioemu2/`, ensuring robust unit, integration, and regression testing across all foundational subsystems. The suite uses `pytest` as its runner and relies on dedicated fixtures and molecular assets to validate model architectures, diffusion samplers, context-parallel execution, structure building, and MSA data pipelines.

Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:38-39](), [DEVELOPER.md:25-29]()

---

## 1. Test Directory Architecture and Source Mirroring

The `tests/` directory layout maps directly to the functional modules inside `src/bioemu2/`. This parallel design makes it straightforward to locate relevant tests when modifying source modules such as `biomoa`, `denoising`, `steering`, `structure`, `msa`, `context_parallel`, and `core`.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        A["Test Suite Root"]
        B["BioMoA Model Tests"]
        C["Denoising & Steering Tests"]
        D["Structure & CCD Tests"]
        E["Context Parallel Tests"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        F["tests/"] --> G["tests/biomoa/"]
        F --> H["tests/denoising/"]
        F --> I["tests/steering/"]
        F --> J["tests/structure/"]
        F --> K["tests/ccd/"]
        F --> L["tests/context_parallel/"]
        F --> M["tests/msa/"]
        F --> N["tests/core/"]
    end

    A -.-> F
    B -.-> G
    C -.-> H
    C -.-> I
    D -.-> J
    D -.-> K
    E -.-> L
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:38-39](), [DEVELOPER.md:25-29]()

---

## 2. Core, BioMoA, and Module Verification

The core infrastructure and BioMoA score model stack are tested under `tests/biomoa/` and `tests/core/`. These tests validate tensor shapes, precision handling (`bf16-mixed`), embedders, encoders, pair mixers, and foundational operator layers.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        O["Score Model Validation"]
        P["Core Operators"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        Q["tests/biomoa/test_score_model.py"] --> R["src/bioemu2/biomoa/score_model.py"]
        S["tests/core/test_operators.py"] --> T["src/bioemu2/core/"]
    end

    O -.-> Q
    P -.-> S
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:38-39](), [DEVELOPER.md:25-29]()

---

## 3. Denoising, Steering, and Context-Parallel Testing

Subsystems responsible for sampling, inference-time steering potentials, and multi-GPU context parallelism have dedicated test modules under `tests/denoising/`, `tests/steering/`, and `tests/context_parallel/`. These ensure numerical stability, EDM sampler correctness, and proper inter-rank communication sharding.

Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:38-39](), [DEVELOPER.md:25-29]()

---

## 4. Structure, CCD, and MSA Pipelines

Structure generation, chemical component dictionary (CCD) data parsing, template alignment, and MSA embedding reuse workflows are tested under `tests/structure/`, `tests/ccd/`, and `tests/msa/`. These tests verify coordinate atom gathering, polymer building, and CIF/PDB round-trip integrity.

Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:38-39](), [DEVELOPER.md:25-29]()

---

## 5. Fixtures, Assets, and CI Integration

The test suite relies on shared pytest fixtures and regression test assets (such as sample input configurations, small PDB files, and cached MSA features) to execute deterministically. 

As defined in the continuous integration workflow, tests are executed automatically across multiple Python versions using `uv run`:

```yaml
- name: Run tests
  run: uv run pytest tests -v
```

Developers can run the full suite locally using standard development environments or specific CUDA configurations:

```bash
uv run pytest tests
```

Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:38-39](), [DEVELOPER.md:25-29]()

---

# Page: Code Quality Tooling

# Code Quality Tooling

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.gitignore](.gitignore)
- [.pre-commit-config.yaml](.pre-commit-config.yaml)
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)
- [scripts/generate_docs_toc.py](scripts/generate_docs_toc.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This page documents the code quality tooling, static analysis configurations, pre-commit automation, project build specifications, and ignore conventions used across the BioEmu2 repository. It details how tools like Ruff, Mypy, and custom scripts enforce coding standards and formatting rules.

Sources: `[.pre-commit-config.yaml:1-42]()`, `[pyproject.toml:1-152]()`, `[scripts/generate_docs_toc.py:1-98]()`, `[.gitignore:1-219]()`

## Pre-Commit Automation Workflow
BioEmu2 uses `pre-commit` to run checks and formatters automatically before commits are finalized. The configuration is defined in `[.pre-commit-config.yaml:1-42]()`.

### Pre-Commit Hook Stages
The pre-commit pipeline executes local and remote hooks in sequence:
1. **Documentation TOC Generation**: Runs a local Python script `[scripts/generate_docs_toc.py:1-98]()` matching markdown files in `docs/`.
2. **Standard Repository Checks**: Uses `pre-commit-hooks` to catch debugging statements and prevent committing oversized files above 500 KB via `[.pre-commit-config.yaml:10-18]()`.
3. **Ruff Formatting and Linting**: Uses `ruff-pre-commit` to format Python code (`ruff-format`) and perform fast lint checks (`ruff-check`) with auto-fix capabilities on `[src/]()` and `[tests/]()` (`[.pre-commit-config.yaml:19-28]()`).
4. **Mypy Static Type Checking**: Runs static type analysis using `mirrors-mypy` under Python 3.12 with stubs for PyYAML and requests (`[.pre-commit-config.yaml:29-42]()`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["DeveloperCommit"] --> B["PreCommitRunner"]
    B --> C["generate-docs-toc\nscripts/generate_docs_toc.py"]
    B --> D["debug-statements\npre-commit-hooks"]
    B --> E["check-added-large-files\npre-commit-hooks"]
    B --> F["ruff-format\nruff-pre-commit"]
    B --> G["ruff-check\nruff-pre-commit"]
    B --> H["mypy\nmirrors-mypy"]
    
    C --> I["MarkdownDocs"]
    F --> J["FormattedPythonCode"]
    G --> K["LintedPythonCode"]
    H --> L["TypeCheckedCode"]
```
*Figure 1: Pre-commit pipeline execution flow linking configuration hooks to validation targets.*

Sources: `[.pre-commit-config.yaml:1-42]()`, `[scripts/generate_docs_toc.py:1-98]()`

## Documentation TOC Generation Tool
To keep extensive markdown documentation in `docs/` organized, BioEmu2 includes an automated TOC generator script located at `[scripts/generate_docs_toc.py:1-98]()`.

### Key Functions
- `_without_toc(text: str) -> str`: Removes existing generated TOC blocks bracketed by `<!-- BEGIN GENERATED TOC -->` and `<!-- END GENERATED TOC -->` (`[scripts/generate_docs_toc.py:17-22]()`).
- `_headings(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, str]]`: Parses markdown headings (level 2 to 4) while ignoring code fences (`[scripts/generate_docs_toc.py:25-37]()`).
- `_anchor(title: str, counts: dict[str, int]) -> str`: Generates URL-safe slugs for headings, handling duplicates by appending numerical suffixes (`[scripts/generate_docs_toc.py:40-51]()`).
- `_render_toc(headings: list[tuple[int, str]]) -> str`: Renders the Markdown unordered list of links representing the table of contents (`[scripts/generate_docs_toc.py:54-68]()`).
- `update(path: Path) -> None`: Conditionally updates files if they exceed `MIN_LINES` (200 lines) or `MIN_SECTIONS` (6 sections) (`[scripts/generate_docs_toc.py:80-94]()`).

```mermaid
graph TD
    M["MarkdownFile\ndocs/*.md"] --> U["update\nscripts/generate_docs_toc.py:80"]
    U --> W["_without_toc\nscripts/generate_docs_toc.py:17"]
    W --> H["_headings\nscripts/generate_docs_toc.py:25"]
    H --> R["_render_toc\nscripts/generate_docs_toc.py:54"]
    R --> A["_anchor\nscripts/generate_docs_toc.py:40"]
    R --> I["_insert_after_title\nscripts/generate_docs_toc.py:71"]
    I --> M
```
*Figure 2: Data flow for the documentation TOC generator script.*

Sources: `[scripts/generate_docs_toc.py:1-98]()`

## Project and Linter Configuration (`pyproject.toml`)
Project metadata, dependencies, optional packages, and tool configurations are centralized in `[pyproject.toml:1-152]()`.

### Ruff Configuration
Ruff is configured with a line length of 100 characters targeting Python 3.12 (`[pyproject.toml:120-122]()`). 
- **Formatting**: Uses double quotes, space indentation, and preserves magic trailing commas (`[pyproject.toml:124-128]()`).
- **Linting Selectors**: Selects rules `E`, `W`, `F`, `UP` (pyupgrade), `PLE`, `PLC0415`, and `I` (isort) (`[pyproject.toml:130-139]()`).
- **Ignores**: Ignores specific lint rules like `W605`, `E501`, `E402`, `E741`, and `UP007` (`[pyproject.toml:140-146]()`).
- **Isort**: Treats `bioemu2` as a known first-party package (`[pyproject.toml:149-151]()`).

### Pytest Options
Test markers are registered under `[tool.pytest.ini_options:112-118]()`, including `gpu`, `requires_4gpu`, `slow`, and `serial`.

Sources: `[pyproject.toml:1-152]()`

## Git Ignore Conventions
The `.gitignore` file (`[.gitignore:1-219]()`) defines exclusions for build artifacts, temporary files, editor settings, and large model outputs.

### Key Excluded Categories
- **IDE and Editor Configs**: `.vscode/`, `.cursor/`, `.idea/`, `.run/` (`[.gitignore:8-19]()`).
- **Python Bytecode and Packaging**: `__pycache__/`, `*.py[cod]`, `build/`, `dist/`, `*.egg-info/` (`[.gitignore:23-47]()`).
- **Test and Coverage Reports**: `htmlcov/`, `.tox/`, `.coverage`, `.pytest_cache/` (`[.gitignore:60-73]()`).
- **Environment Directories**: `.env`, `.venv/`, `env/`, `venv/`, `.pixi/` (`[.gitignore:136-144]()`).
- **Tool Caches**: `.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/` (`[.gitignore:156-162]()`).
- **Model Outputs and Checkpoints**: `**/outputs/`, `**/testdata/`, `*.pt`, `*.pth`, `*.ckpt`, `.data/` (`[.gitignore:173-182]()`).

Sources: `[.gitignore:1-219]()`

# Page: CI Workflows and Release Publishing

# CI Workflows and Release Publishing

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/dependabot.yml](.github/dependabot.yml)
- [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml)
- [.github/workflows/publish-pages.yml](.github/workflows/publish-pages.yml)
- [.github/workflows/publish.yml](.github/workflows/publish.yml)

</details>



This page details the Continuous Integration (CI), automated release publishing, GitHub Pages deployment, and dependency management infrastructure defined in the GitHub Actions workflows and configuration files of the BioEmu2 repository.

---

## 1. Continuous Integration Matrix (`ci.yml`)

The primary CI pipeline is defined in [.github/workflows/ci.yml:1-39]() and runs automated checks across multiple Python versions on pull requests and pushes to the `main` branch.

### Workflow Triggers and Concurrency
The CI workflow is triggered by pushes to `main`, pull requests, and manual dispatches [.github/workflows/ci.yml:3-8](). Concurrency groups are configured to cancel in-progress runs for pull requests while preserving runs on `main` [.github/workflows/ci.yml:10-12]().

### Job Matrix and Setup
The `test` job runs on `ubuntu-latest` and utilizes a matrix strategy across Python versions `"3.12"`, `"3.13"`, and `"3.14"` [.github/workflows/ci.yml:18-23](). 
1. **Environment Setup**: Actions check out the repository [.github/workflows/ci.yml:27]() and configure Python [.github/workflows/ci.yml:28-30]().
2. **Package Manager**: Installs `uv==0.11.0` via `pip` [.github/workflows/ci.yml:31-32]().
3. **Dependency Synchronization**: Synchronizes environment dependencies locked to the repository state with the `dev` extra enabled using `uv sync --locked --extra dev` [.github/workflows/ci.yml:33-34]().

### Linter, Type Check, and Test Execution
* **Pre-commit Checks**: Formatting, linting, and type checking (`ruff`, `mypy`) are executed via `uv run pre-commit run --verbose --all-files`, restricted conditionally to Python version `'3.12'` [.github/workflows/ci.yml:35-37]().
* **Test Suite**: Executes the test runner using `uv run pytest tests -v` across all matrix Python versions [.github/workflows/ci.yml:38-39]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "CI Workflow Execution (.github/workflows/ci.yml)"
      A["push / pull_request / workflow_dispatch"] --> B["test job [ubuntu-latest]"]
      B --> C["Matrix Python: 3.12, 3.13, 3.14"]
      C --> D["Install uv==0.11.0"]
      D --> E["uv sync --locked --extra dev"]
      E --> F{"matrix.python-version == '3.12'?"}
      F -- Yes --> G["uv run pre-commit run --verbose --all-files"]
      F -- No --> H["Skip Linter/Types"]
      G --> I["uv run pytest tests -v"]
      H --> I
    end
```
*Sources: [.github/workflows/ci.yml:1-39]()*

---

## 2. Release Publishing and Trusted Publishing (`publish.yml`)

Automated packaging and distribution to PyPI upon publishing a release is configured in [.github/workflows/publish.yml:1-57](). It uses a two-job pipeline (`build` followed by `publish`) implementing OpenID Connect (OIDC) trusted publishing.

### Build Job
The `build` job runs on `ubuntu-latest` with Python `3.12` [.github/workflows/publish.yml:11-21]():
1. **Tag Validation**: Compares the GitHub release tag (`${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}`) against the version reported by `uv version --short` from `pyproject.toml`, failing the build if a mismatch is detected [.github/workflows/publish.yml:25-33]().
2. **Distribution Generation**: Builds source and binary distributions using `uv build` [.github/workflows/publish.yml:34-35]().
3. **Distribution Verification**: Validates built distributions against strict specifications using `uvx twine==6.2.0 check --strict dist/*` [.github/workflows/publish.yml:36-37]().
4. **Artifact Upload**: Uploads the `dist/` directory as a workflow artifact named `dist` [.github/workflows/publish.yml:38-42]().

### Publish Job
The `publish` job depends on the successful completion of the `build` job and executes in the `publish-to-pypi` GitHub environment [.github/workflows/publish.yml:44-47]():
1. **Permissions**: Grants `id-token: write` permissions required for OIDC trusted publishing with PyPI [.github/workflows/publish.yml:48-49]().
2. **Artifact Retrieval**: Downloads the built distributions artifact [.github/workflows/publish.yml:51-55]().
3. **PyPI Upload**: Publishes the package using `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` [.github/workflows/publish.yml:56-57]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Release Publishing Pipeline (.github/workflows/publish.yml)"
      A["release [published]"] --> B["job: build [ubuntu-latest, python-3.12]"]
      B --> C["Check release tag matches pyproject.toml version"]
      C --> D["uv build"]
      D --> E["uvx twine==6.2.0 check --strict dist/*"]
      E --> F["Upload artifact: dist"]
      F --> G["job: publish [environment: publish-to-pypi]"]
      G --> H["Download artifact: dist"]
      H --> I["pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish [id-token: write]"]
    end
```
*Sources: [.github/workflows/publish.yml:1-57]()*

---

## 3. GitHub Pages Deployment (`publish-pages.yml`)

The workflow for publishing notebook and static documentation pages is defined in [.github/workflows/publish-pages.yml:1-36]().

### Execution Flow
* **Trigger**: Activated exclusively via manual workflow dispatch (`workflow_dispatch`) [.github/workflows/publish.yml:3-4]().
* **Concurrency**: Grouped under `github-pages` with `cancel-in-progress: false` [.github/workflows/publish-pages.yml:6-8]().
* **Permissions**: Requires `contents: read`, `pages: write`, and `id-token: write` [.github/workflows/publish-pages.yml:10-14]().
* **Deployment Steps**:
  1. Checks out the `pages` branch into a local `site` directory using `actions/checkout` [.github/workflows/publish-pages.yml:22-27]().
  2. Configures GitHub Pages via `actions/configure-pages` [.github/workflows/publish.yml:28-29]().
  3. Uploads the static site artifact using `actions/upload-pages-artifact` [.github/workflows/publish.yml:30-33]().
  4. Deploys to GitHub Pages via `actions/deploy-pages` [.github/workflows/publish.yml:34-36]().

*Sources: [.github/workflows/publish-pages.yml:1-36]()*

---

## 4. Automated Dependency Maintenance (`dependabot.yml`)

Dependency updates are automated via Dependabot configuration in [.github/dependabot.yml:1-22](). 

### Ecosystem Configuration
Dependabot tracks three package ecosystems on a weekly schedule with a 14-day cooldown period for updates:
* **`uv`**: Manages Python dependencies rooted at `/` [.github/dependabot.yml:3-8]().
* **`github-actions`**: Manages GitHub Actions workflow action versions rooted at `/` [.github/dependabot.yml:10-15]().
* **`pre-commit`**: Manages pre-commit hook versions rooted at `/` [.github/dependabot.yml:17-22]().

*Sources: [.github/dependabot.yml:1-22]()*

---

# Page: Contributing and Governance

# Contributing and Governance

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope
This section outlines the community guidelines, contribution pathways, licensing requirements, code of conduct, and security reporting policies for the `bioemu2` repository. BioEmu2 welcomes community participation, bug reports, feature proposals, and code contributions under structured governance policies established for Microsoft open-source repositories.

Sources: [CONTRIBUTING.md:1-11](), [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md:1-10](), [SECURITY.md:1-14]()

---

## Contributor License Agreement (CLA) Process
All external code contributions and substantial suggestions to BioEmu2 require agreement to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA). This process ensures that contributors retain copyright while granting Microsoft the necessary rights to use, modify, and distribute the contribution.

When a contributor opens a pull request, an automated CLA bot inspects the PR status [CONTRIBUTING.md:9-10]():
1. **Verification**: The bot checks whether the author has previously signed the Microsoft open-source CLA.
2. **Instructions**: If unsigned, the bot posts a comment containing instructions and a link to complete the agreement at [https://cla.opensource.microsoft.com](https://cla.opensource.microsoft.com) [CONTRIBUTING.md:6-10]().
3. **Scope**: Contributors only need to sign the CLA once across all repositories utilizing the Microsoft CLA infrastructure [CONTRIBUTING.md:10-11]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    PR["User opens pull request"] --> CLABot["CLA Bot evaluation"]
    CLABot --> IsSigned{"Already signed?"}
    IsSigned -- "Yes" --> Ready["PR ready for review"]
    IsSigned -- "No" --> Prompt["Post signing instructions link"]
    Prompt --> Sign["User signs at cla.opensource.microsoft.com"]
    Sign --> Ready
```
*Figure 1: The automated Contributor License Agreement (CLA) verification workflow upon opening a pull request.*

Sources: [CONTRIBUTING.md:1-11]()

---

## Pull Request Workflow
Proposing changes to BioEmu2 follows standard GitHub fork-and-pull workflows. Contributors are encouraged to open a pull request to initiate discussion and code review for any proposed changes [CONTRIBUTING.md:3-4]().

- **Proposal**: Changes should be submitted via a pull request against the main repository branches [CONTRIBUTING.md:3-4]().
- **Automated Checks**: PRs trigger automated validation pipelines (such as linting, formatting checks, and test suites) to maintain code quality across the codebase.
- **Review**: Maintainers evaluate pull requests for functional correctness, adherence to code quality tooling, and alignment with the BioEmu2 foundation model design.

Sources: [CONTRIBUTING.md:1-4]()

---

## Code of Conduct
BioEmu2 has adopted the official Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md:1-3](). This policy defines expected behavior, inclusivity standards, and anti-harassment rules for all community spaces, issues, pull requests, and communications.

- **Primary Resources**: 
  - [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/) [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md:3-7]()
  - [Microsoft Code of Conduct FAQ](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/faq/) [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md:8]()
- **Reporting Concerns**: 
  - General questions or concerns regarding conduct can be directed to `opencode@microsoft.com` [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md:9]().
  - Internal Microsoft employees can reach out via `aka.ms/opensource/moderation-support` [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md:10]().

```mermaid
graph TD
    Issue["Community / Conduct Issue"] --> ContactChoice{"User type?"}
    ContactChoice -- "External Contributor" --> Email["Email opencode@microsoft.com"]
    ContactChoice -- "Microsoft Employee" --> Internal["Visit aka.ms/opensource/moderation-support"]
    Email --> Resolution["Moderation and Support Review"]
    Internal --> Resolution
```
*Figure 2: Escalation pathways for code of conduct violations and moderation support.*

Sources: [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md:1-10]()

---

## Security Reporting
Microsoft takes the security of software products, services, and source code repositories seriously [SECURITY.md:5-6](). 

- **Vulnerability Reporting Policy**: **Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues [SECURITY.md:8]().** Public disclosures before a fix is available put users at risk.
- **Reporting Channels**: For security reporting guidelines, vulnerability disclosure instructions, and contact details, review the guidance maintained at [https://aka.ms/SECURITY.md](https://aka.ms/SECURITY.md) [SECURITY.md:10-12]().

Sources: [SECURITY.md:1-14]()
